Assessment of right ventricular function by echocardiography was performed at admission and again at the switch to oral diuretics. Telephone follow-up was scheduled at 3 months and 12 months after hospital discharge
primary_outcomes: death or new onset acute failure

brief_summary: This clinical trial is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-design phase 3 clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Bronpass Tab. in 146 patients with symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in CAT total score at each visit
title: Study to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of Bronpass Tab. in Patients With Symptoms of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effects of cervical proprioceptive training, with or without vestibular rehabilitation, in patients with cervicogenic dizziness. Cervicogenic dizziness is a condition in which problems involving the neck may contribute to dizziness, neck pain, and difficulties with balance.

The study will include adults aged 20-40 years who experience chronic neck pain and dizziness associated with neck movements. A total of 58 participants will be recruited and randomly allocated into two groups.

Participants in Group A will receive vestibular rehabilitation combined with cervical proprioceptive training, while participants in Group B will receive vestibular rehabilitation alone. Both groups will attend supervised treatment sessions three times per week for eight weeks and will also follow a home exercise programme.

The study will assess dizziness, neck pain, disability, cervical joint position sense, and balance. These outcomes will be measured before treatment, after four weeks, and after eight weeks using standardized assessment tools, including the Dizziness Handicap Inventory, Neck Disability Index, Visual Analogue Scale, Joint Position Error Test, and Berg Balance Scale.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether adding cervical proprioceptive training to vestibular rehabilitation produces greater improvements in dizziness, neck pain, disability, and balance than vestibular rehabilitation alone.

The findings may help physiotherapists understand the role of these rehabilitation approaches and support the development of more effective treatment programmes for people experiencing cervicogenic dizziness.
interventions: Vestibular Rehabilitation Therapy (VRT) with Cervical Proprioceptive Training (CPT)
primary_outcomes: Change in Dizziness-Related Disability Measured by the Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI)
title: Effects of Cervical Proprioceptive Training With or Without Vestibular Rehabilitation in Patients With Cervicogenic Dizziness

brief_summary: This randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluates the safety and preliminary efficacy of AdiaVita (umbilical cord blood-derived stem cell and exosome product) compared with saline placebo in children aged 3-12 years with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Approximately 100 participants will be enrolled at two sites and randomly assigned 1:1 to receive three monthly intravenous infusions of either AdiaVita or saline placebo. The primary outcome is the change in parent-reported Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist (ATEC) total score from baseline to Month 3. After the Month 3 assessment, eligible participants who received placebo may cross over to receive AdiaVita. All participants are followed through Month 12 for safety and additional outcome assessments. AdiaVita is not FDA-approved for the treatment of ASD.
interventions: Umbilical Cord Blood-Derived Stem Cells and Exosomes
lead_sponsor: Adia Med of Winter Park LLC
primary_outcomes: Change in Parent-Reported Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist (ATEC) Total Score from Baseline to Month 3

brief_summary:
This prospective clinical study aims to evaluate the diagnostic value of a GPC3-targeted imaging agent for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

A total of 30 adults with clinically or histopathologically diagnosed HCC will be enrolled. Each participant will undergo two PET examinations, one using the GPC3-targeted imaging agent and the other using 18F-FDG, within an interval of five days.

The study will compare the diagnostic performance of the two imaging methods for detecting HCC lesions. Diagnostic accuracy will be evaluated using histopathological findings or clinical and imaging follow-up as the reference standard.

The study will also assess imaging characteristics, safety, the relationship between GPC3-targeted imaging agent uptake and tumor GPC3 expression, and the potential impact of the imaging findings on disease staging and clinical management.
primary_outcomes: Lesion-Level Diagnostic Sensitivity of GPC3-Targeted PET and 18F-FDG PET
Lesion-Level Diagnostic Specificity of GPC3-Targeted PET and 18F-FDG PET
Lesion-Level Diagnostic Accuracy of GPC3-Targeted PET and 18F-FDG PET
Lesion-Level Positive Predictive Value of GPC3-Targeted PET and 18F-FDG PET
Lesion-Level Negative Predictive Value of GPC3-Targeted PET and 18F-FDG PET
title: GPC3-Targeted PET Imaging for the Diagnosis of Hepatocellular Carcinoma

brief_summary:
This study investigated whether adding digital technologies to graded motor imagery (GMI) rehabilitation could improve upper limb motor function and daily activities in people recovering from stroke.

GMI is a rehabilitation approach that uses several techniques to support movement recovery, including recognizing images of left and right hands, imagining movements, observing actions, and mirror therapy.

A total of 24 adults in the subacute phase after stroke participated in this randomized controlled trial. Participants were assigned to one of two groups. Both groups received GMI combined with upper limb mobilization, relaxation exercises, and task-oriented training. The experimental group performed GMI activities using digital technologies, including a hand laterality recognition application, augmented reality, and video-based mirror therapy. The control group performed comparable activities using conventional materials and techniques.

Both groups received 36 individual rehabilitation sessions over 12 weeks, with three sessions per week.

The main outcome was upper limb motor function, assessed using the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the Upper Extremity (FMA-UE). Additional assessments examined independence in daily activities, arm use, occupational performance, quality of life, and motor imagery ability.

The study aimed to determine whether technology-assisted GMI provided additional benefits compared with conventional GMI in people recovering from stroke.
primary_outcomes: Change in Upper Extremity Motor Function (FMA-UE)
title: Graded Motor Imagery and Virtual Reality for Upper Limb Rehabilitation After Stroke

brief_summary: Micropigmentation (medical tattooing) can camouflage stable vitiligo lesions that do not respond to conventional treatment, but the pigment often fades unpredictably. This prospective single-arm study will evaluate pigment retention at 2 weeks after micropigmentation in 20 patients with stable vitiligo, and will examine inflammatory and CD8+ T-lymphocyte infiltration in paired skin biopsies taken before and after the procedure. The aim is to assess whether residual local immune activity in clinically stable vitiligo contributes to early pigment loss.
title: Pigment Retention After Micropigmentation in Vitiligo, a Clinico-Immunopathological Study

brief_summary:
This is an open-label, multi-cohort, multi-center Phase Ib/II clinical trial evaluating GB268, a trispecific antibody targeting PD-1, CTLA-4 and VEGF, in subjects with metastatic Stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

The study consists of two phases. Phase Ib (safety lead-in) enrolls previously treated subjects into 3 cohorts: A1 (GB268 + paclitaxel + carboplatin in PD-1/L1-pretreated squamous NSCLC), B1 (GB268 + pemetrexed + carboplatin in PD-1/L1-pretreated driver-gene-negative non-squamous NSCLC), and C1 (GB268 monotherapy in subjects who failed both PD-1/L1 and chemotherapy). A modified 3+3 DLT design with a 21-day DLT observation window will be used. The Data Monitoring and Review Committee (DMRC) will select safe dose(s) to proceed to Phase II expansion.

Phase II includes 3 expansion cohorts for first-line metastatic NSCLC: A2 (GB268 + paclitaxel + carboplatin for squamous NSCLC), B2 (GB268 + pemetrexed + carboplatin for driver-gene-negative non-squamous NSCLC), and C2 (GB268 monotherapy for PD-L1 TPS ≥ 1% NSCLC). Each expansion cohort will enroll up to 60 subjects.

The primary endpoint for Phase Ib is safety and tolerability. The primary endpoint for Phase II is investigator-assessed objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1. Secondary endpoints include PFS, DOR, DCR, TTR, OS, pharmacokinetic profile and immunogenicity. Exploratory objectives evaluate PD-L1 and other blood/tumor-derived predictive and resistance biomarkers.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with adverse events [AEs](Phase Ib)
title: GB268 Alone or in Combination for Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
This is an observational study in which data already collected from people in the United States (US) with chronic kidney disease (CKD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) and heart failure (HF) are studied. In observational studies, only observations are made without specified advice or interventions.

The main purpose of this study is to learn how well finerenone works, and to describe its safety, in routine US healthcare for adults who have CKD, T2D, and HF. Researchers will compare people who start finerenone with similar people who do not use finerenone. The participants in this study will have received the study treatment finerenone or a different treatment (for those who do not use finerenone) as part of their regular care as delivered by their treating physicians.

HF happens when the heart cannot pump blood as well as it should. It can cause shortness of breath, tiredness, swelling in the legs or ankles, and hospital stays. CKD means the kidneys are damaged or do not work as well over time. T2D is a condition in which the body has difficulty controlling blood sugar. Having HF, CKD, and T2D together can make each condition worse and can increase the chance of serious heart and kidney problems.

Finerenone works by blocking certain proteins, called mineralocorticoid receptors. By doing this, it may reduce damage to kidneys, heart and blood vessels.

During the study, the researchers will collect general information of the participants such as age or gender and data on kidney function and possible heart problems.

The researchers will also collect data on any other disease or medical condition in the participants and on other medications used while taking finerenone.

The data will come from healthcare claims, electronic health records (EHRs), and laboratory records in the United States. They cover the period from July 9th, 2021 until the latest data cut is available for each dataset. Only already available data is collected and studied. There are no required visits or tests in this study.
primary_outcomes: Time to the first occurrence of composite cardiovascular outcome
title: A Study to Learn More About How Well Finerenone Works in People With Chronic Kidney Disease, Type 2 Diabetes and Heart Failure in Routine Medical Practice in the United States

brief_summary:
Locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC) is commonly treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). Although gemcitabine plus cisplatin (GP) neoadjuvant chemotherapy improves survival, its benefit may be limited in selected patients, while treatment-related toxicities may compromise subsequent CCRT. In a randomized phase III trial, GP neoadjuvant chemotherapy improved 5-year overall survival (OS) in patients with stage III-IVB disease according to the eighth edition of the AJCC/UICC staging system, excluding T3-4N0 disease (87.9% vs 78.8%; hazard ratio \[HR\], 0.51; P=0.001), but not in patients with pretreatment plasma Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA levels below 4000 copies/mL, predominantly those with T1-2N2, T3N1-2, or T4N1 disease (5-year OS, 90.6% vs 91.4%; P=0.77). These findings underscore the need for effective strategies that minimize unnecessary chemotherapy and its associated toxicity while preserving disease control.

In a previous phase II study, neoadjuvant and adjuvant toripalimab combined with CCRT showed promising efficacy and favorable tolerability in LA-NPC patients achieving a 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) rate of 91.8%. These findings support with the great clinical need to futher evaluate this neoadjuvant GP chemotherapy-sparing strategy in patients with low- or intermediate-risk LA-NPC with the aim to reduce the toxicity in neoadjuvant chemotherapy phase.

This randomized, open-label, non-inferiority, phase III, multicenter trial will enroll 384 patients with low- or intermediate-risk LA-NPC, randomized 1:1 to receive either two cycles of neoadjuvant toripalimab followed by CCRT and eight cycles of adjuvant toripalimab, or three cycles of GP neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by CCRT.

The primary endpoint is 2-year PFS. Secondary endpoints include OS, locoregional relapse-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, tumor response, treatment-related toxicity and treatment compliance. The study aims to determine whether a toripalimab alone-based neoadjuvant and adjuvant strategy can provide non-inferior disease control while reducing treatment-related toxicity, compared currently standard regimen -GP neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by CCRT.
interventions: GP induction chemotherapy plus concurrent chemoradiotherapy
title: Neoadjuvant and Adjuvant Toripalimab Plus Chemoradiotherapy Versus GP Chemotherapy Plus Chemoradiotherapy for Low- or Intermediate-Risk Locoregionally Advanced Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma

brief_summary: The Metrix CT/NG/TV Test will be evaluated for use in Non-Laboratory settings in a home testing environment utilizing the clinical study design described herein. The study will take place in simulated home environments which will be set up within or near active clinical settings (e.g., urgent care facilities). This will be a prospective study conducted at three or more investigational sites located within the United States for the clinical validation of the Metrix CT/NG/TV Test for the detection of Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Trichomonas vaginalis from vaginal swab samples. Additional sites may be added to the study in order to meet minimum subject/sample enrollment requirements and geographic prevalence of STIs. Comparator testing will be performed to determine the infection status of each sample for comparison to results generated by the candidate test. The patient infectious status will be determined with two separate FDA-cleared assays for the detection of Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Trichomonas vaginalis.
primary_outcomes: Qualitative Detection of DNA from Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Trichomonas vaginalis, and Measurement of Positive Percent Agreement(PPA)/Sensitivity and Negative Percent Agreement (NPA)/Specificity with FDA-cleared tests
title: Clinical Validation of the Metrix CTNGTV Test

brief_summary:
Objective: This study will be conducted to evaluate the effects of an ehram-woven wool vest on fibromyalgia.

Material and Method: The study population will consist of individuals diagnosed with fibromyalgia. Participants who meet the inclusion criteria will be allocated to the experimental, placebo, and control groups. Participants in the experimental group will be provided with an ehram-woven wool vest, while those in the placebo group will receive a synthetic vest, to be worn for a period of three months. Participants will be followed up throughout the three-month study period. Data will be collected using a sociodemographic and clinical information form, the Revised Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQR) as the primary outcome measure, and the Pressure Pain Threshold (PPT), Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain, Thermal Comfort Scale, 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), and daily assessment form as secondary outcome measures.
title: The Effect of Ehram Woven Wool Vest on Fibromyalgia

brief_summary:
A Phase 2, Multicenter, Open-label, Randomized, Active-Controlled Trial to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of a Single Suprachoroidal Space (SCS) of KH658 in Participants with Diabetic Macular Edema (DME).

KH658 is a gene therapy drug administered by SCS injection, using an AAV8 variant to deliver a gene encoding an anti-VEGF protein, aimed at treating patients with DME and reducing the frequency of injection required.
primary_outcomes: Mean change in BCVA from baseline
title: A Phase II Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of KH658 Gene Therapy in Patients With Diabetic Macular Edema (DME)

brief_summary:
The sniffing position (SP) remains the conventional starting point for direct laryngoscopy. SP is characterised by two components- first, flexion of neck on the chest at lower cervical joint and second, the extension of head-on-neck at the atlanto-occipital joint. While, cervico-thoracic flexion produced by head elevation is passive and has inertia (persists once established), the head-on-neck extension is actively generated and may get easily lost as the operator moves from positioning endpoint to direct laryngoscopy and intubation (DLI) (laryngoscope blade insertion, glottis-inlet visualization, and tracheal intubation). Whereas the SP has been studied for different contexts of upper airway access management; it has never been examined for adequacy of achievement and sustenance of its adequacy endpoint through the performance of DLI. The investigators contend that it's the loss of head-on-neck extension during DLI which compromises the DLI conduct and results in sub optimal view to the vocal cords and the undue physiologic 'harm' (morbidity due to physical dental/ mucosal trauma and acute rise in systolic blood pressure and heart rate or both, due to aggressive laryngoscopy that ensues to compensate for inadequate SP positioning).

This study works on the premise that greater understanding, observation, and application of 'controlled' SP, especially pertaining to its active head-on-neck extension part; will enhance laryngoscopic view to the vocal cords and decrease the attendant morbidity it brings about. This randomised study is set out to evaluate whether the systematic preservation and effective transfer of atlanto-occipital extension into the DLI help achieve improved the first-pass laryngoscopic view and attenuates the post-intubation haemodynamic response.
primary_outcomes: Haemodynamic response upon direct laryngoscopy and tracheal intubation
title: Effect of Controlled Head-on-Neck Extension ON Laryngoscopy and Intubation

brief_summary:
This first-in-human, single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase I dose-escalation trial evaluates the tolerability, safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), and immunogenicity of injectable VDJ006 (a long-acting IL-1 receptor antagonist) given by intravenous infusion to healthy Chinese subjects. It includes a single-ascending-dose (SAD) part with 28 subjects across five cohorts (1, 2, 6, 9, 12 mg/kg) and a multiple-ascending-dose (MAD) part with 16 subjects across two cohorts (6, 9 mg/kg) receiving weekly IV infusion for 4 weeks, with dose escalation governed by predefined CTCAE 6.0 stopping rules.

The primary objective is to assess the safety and tolerability of single and multiple VDJ006 doses; secondary objectives are to characterize its PK profile and immunogenicity (anti-drug and neutralizing antibodies). The study targets cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes (CAPS), an IL-1β-driven autoinflammatory disease for which VDJ006 offers a novel, long-acting IL-1 blockade option.
primary_outcomes: Absolute eosinophil count (Eo) assessed by automated hematology analyzer
Urine red blood cells assessed by automated urinalysis analyzer
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) assessed by clinical chemistry analyzer
title: VDJ006 for Injection in Healthy Subjects

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to evaluate the effects of a midwife-supported education program timed according to the menstrual cycle on premenstrual syndrome (PMS) symptoms and quality of life in young women. The study will also examine the program's effect on attitudes toward menstruation and the relationship between PMS symptom severity and quality of life.

The study will include 96 young women aged 18-29 years attending Family Health Centers in the district center of Elbistan, Türkiye. Participants will be randomly assigned to an education group or a control group, with 48 participants in each group.

The education group will receive four face-to-face educational sessions delivered by the researcher, who is a midwife, over 15 days. All participants in this group will receive the same educational content. Whenever possible, the program will begin shortly after menstrual bleeding has ended, with the aim of completing the program before the next menstrual period begins. The sessions will cover the menstrual cycle, PMS symptoms, attitudes toward menstruation, self-care, healthy lifestyle habits, and stress management. Participants in the control group will receive no study-provided education or educational materials during the study.

Assessments in both groups will be conducted at baseline, at the end of the 15-day education period, at the end of the first menstrual period following completion of the education program, and at the end of the second menstrual period following program completion.

The researchers hypothesize that the education program will reduce PMS symptom severity and improve quality of life compared with the control group.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Premenstrual Symptom Severity
title: EFFECTS OF A MIDWIFE-SUPPORTED EDUCATION PROGRAM ON PREMENSTRUAL SYMPTOMS, ATTITUDES TOWARD MENSTRUATION, AND QUALITY OF LIFE IN YOUNG WOMEN: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare two transcatheter heart valves, the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA and the SAPIEN 3 Ultra, in adults with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis (narrowing of the aortic valve) who are undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a 23 mm valve.

The main question it aims to answer is:

* Does the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA valve allow blood to flow more easily through the valve than the SAPIEN 3 Ultra valve after TAVR?

Researchers will compare participants who receive the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA valve with those who receive the SAPIEN 3 Ultra valve to see if there are differences in how blood flows through the valves after implantation.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA or SAPIEN 3 Ultra valve during their clinically indicated TAVR procedure.
interventions: SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA Transcatheter Heart Valve (23 mm)
SAPIEN 3 Ultra Transcatheter Heart Valve (23 mm)
primary_outcomes: Invasive Aortic Valve Mean Gradient After TAVR (mmHg)
title: Randomized Assessment of SAPIEN 3 Ultra and SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA Valve 23 in Patients With Severe Aortic Stenosis

title: Phase III Trial of SK3530 in Erectile Dysfunction

brief_summary: This completed study compared rehabilitation alone with rehabilitation plus procaine neural therapy in adults who had experienced a stroke at least one month earlier. Neural therapy involved injections of procaine, a local anesthetic, during three weekly treatment sessions. The study examined changes in general pain and independence in everyday activities. Sixty-one participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups were prescribed the same three-week rehabilitation program, followed by home exercises. Pain and functional independence were assessed before treatment, after the three-week course, and three months after the course ended. The outcome analysis included the 50 participants who completed all assessments. This record is being entered after the study was completed.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in General Pain Intensity at Three Months After Treatment
Change From Baseline in Functional Independence Measure Total Score at Three Months After Treatment
title: Procaine Neural Therapy Added to Rehabilitation After Stroke

brief_summary: Children and adolescents with unilateral cerebral palsy often receive botulinum toxin type A injections in the upper limb to reduce spasticity. In usual care in Spain, rehabilitation after the injection is not standardized: what each child receives varies, and it is common to provide only written home recommendations based mainly on stretching. Little is known about whether a structured home program can be carried out by families and how it compares with that usual care. This pilot randomized trial will test the feasibility, family adherence, acceptability and safety of a 10-week home-based program of functional strength and goal-directed training that starts shortly after the injection, compared with usual home-based care. Participants aged 6 to 18 years who are scheduled for an injection as part of usual care are randomly assigned (1:1) to the structured program (45 minutes a day, 5 days a week, with weekly remote supervision) or to usual care (written recommendations). Assessments take place before the injection and 6-8 weeks and 12 weeks after it. Because this is a pilot, the trial is not designed to show that one approach is better than the other. It will also provide preliminary estimates of change in upper-limb function, including with the Spanish version of the Shriners Hospital for Children Upper Extremity Evaluation (sp-SHUEE), to plan a later definitive trial.
interventions: Structured home-based functional strength and goal-directed program
title: Home-Based Functional Strength and Goal-Directed Training After Botulinum Toxin in Children With Unilateral Cerebral Palsy.

brief_summary: The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the differences in weight-loss efficacy, safety, and tolerability of different doses of HSK55879 tablets administered once daily for 26 consecutive weeks versus placebo in participants with overweight/obesity.
title: A Phase II Clinical Study of HSK55879 Tablets in Participants With Overweight or Obesity

brief_summary:
Lumbar radiculopathy is a condition in which irritation or compression of nerves in the lower back can cause pain that travels into the legs. People with this condition may also experience difficulty moving, reduced range of motion, limitations in daily activities, and a lower quality of life.

The purpose of this study is to compare the effects of low-intensity laser therapy alone with a combination of low-intensity laser therapy and neurodynamic mobilization in patients with lumbar radiculopathy.

This study will include 58 patients diagnosed with lumbar radiculopathy who meet the eligibility criteria. Participants will be randomly divided into two groups. Group A will receive low-intensity laser therapy, while Group B will receive low-intensity laser therapy combined with neurodynamic mobilization. Both groups will receive treatment three times per week for four weeks.

The study will assess pain intensity, range of motion, functional disability, and quality of life. Pain will be measured using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale, range of motion using a goniometer, functional disability using the Oswestry Disability Index, and quality of life using the 12-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12).

Assessments will be conducted at baseline, after four weeks of treatment, and at an eight-week follow-up. The findings will help determine whether combining neurodynamic mobilization with laser therapy provides greater improvement in pain, movement, daily functioning, and quality of life than laser therapy alone.
title: Effects of Neurodynamic Mobilization With and Without Laser Therapy in Patients With Lumbar Radiculopathy

brief_summary:
This is a phase II, single-arm, multicenter study designed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who achieve a major pathological response (MPR) and have negative circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) after neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy and complete surgical resection.

Eligible patients who achieve MPR, defined as 10% or less residual viable tumor cells, and have negative ctDNA results 21-30 days after surgery will undergo observation without postoperative adjuvant therapy.

The study plans to enroll 88 patients across three centers in China. Participants will undergo regular imaging examinations and ctDNA monitoring for two years after surgery.

The primary outcome is the 2-year event-free survival (EFS) rate. Secondary and exploratory objectives include evaluating the prognostic value of ctDNA monitoring and investigating associations between tumor microenvironment characteristics and clinical outcomes.

This study aims to explore whether postoperative observation without adjuvant treatment is a feasible strategy for selected patients with favorable pathological and molecular responses to neoadjuvant therapy.
title: Postoperative Outcomes Without Adjuvant Therapy in NSCLC Patients With MPR and Negative ctDNA After Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy

brief_summary: This study aims to conduct a multicenter, bidirectional, observational study by enrolling patients with hematological malignancies diagnosed with CNS-IMD and receiving esconazole as first-line treatment at 12 hematological disease research centers in China from September 2022 to December 2026. The outcome measures of this study were the efficacy (all-cause mortality, fungal infection-related mortality and overall response rate) and safety (incidence of treatment-related adverse events) of initial treatment with esaconazole in patients with CNS-IMD. All-cause mortality refers to the overall mortality rate of patients at 42 days of treatment with esconazole. Fungal infection-related mortality refers to the proportion of deaths directly attributed to fungal infections. Based on clinical, imaging and microbiological results, the treatment response rates of patients at 4, 6 and 12 weeks were evaluated.
title: Clinical Characteristics and Prognosis of Invasive Mycosis of the Central Nervous System

brief_summary: This pilot study evaluated whether a non-pesticidal head lice treatment kit that works by mechanical action could clear head lice infestations in children and adults. The kit includes a gel containing mild natural abrasives (walnut shell powder and diatomaceous earth), an applicator brush, a removal shampoo gel, a metal lice comb, and a magnifier. Study staff applied the treatment to 26 participants aged 3 to 70 years at a community center in Homestead, Florida. Participants who still had live lice one week later received a second treatment. The main outcome was the proportion of participants with no live lice and no viable nits two weeks after the first treatment. The study also recorded how long treatment took and whether any scalp or eye irritation or other adverse events occurred.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants free of live lice and viable nits at Day 15
title: Mechanically Acting Lice Treatment Kit in Children and Adults With Head Lice

brief_summary: To compare the efficacy and safety of nebulized dexmedetomidine versus nebulized midazolam for sedation quality and on gag reflex in adult patients undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, to determine which agent provides better suppression of gagging, superior sedation quality, patient comfort and satisfaction, hemodynamic and respiratory stability, with fewer side effects
primary_outcomes: Gag reflex severity assessed using the 0-3-point Gag Reflex Grading Scale 0: No gagging 1: Mild gagging (1-2 episodes) 2: Moderate gagging (3-4 episodes) 3: Severe gagging (more than 5 episodes)
title: Gag Reflex and Sedation Quality Using Nebulized Dexmedetomidine Versus Nebulized Midazolam During Upper Gastrointestinal Endoscopy

brief_summary: The REA study is a prospective, decentralized observational study investigating insulin infusion set failures in adults with type 1 diabetes using the myLoop system. During the three-month study period, participants will collect up to three failed infusion sets and corresponding control sets, while providing CGM and insulin pump data. The study aims to identify factors associated with infusion set failures under real-world conditions.
primary_outcomes: Difference in Cannula Proteomic Profiles Between Failed and Non-Failed Infusion Sets
title: A Real-world Evaluation of Insulin Infusion Set Failures

brief_summary:
This observational pilot study aims to compare perioperative analgesic strategies and opioid consumption in adult patients undergoing single-port (SP) versus multi-port (MP) robot-assisted urologic surgery, including prostatectomy and nephrectomy.

The primary objective is to compare total opioid consumption, expressed in morphine milligram equivalents (MME), from the intraoperative period up to 24 hours after surgery.

Secondary objectives include the assessment of postoperative pain intensity, perioperative analgesic management, postoperative complications, and length of hospital stay.

The study will be conducted at Erasme University Hospital in Brussels, Belgium, and will include both retrospective and prospective data collection.

As this is a non-interventional study, surgical and anesthetic management will follow routine clinical practice, without any additional procedures imposed by the study protocol.
title: Comparison of Perioperative Analgesia in Single-Port Versus Multi-Port Robot-assisted Urologic Surgery

brief_summary: This study evaluates a discharge-linked oral function care protocol for middle-aged and older stroke patients during transition from hospital to home. The primary objective is to evaluate the effects of structured oral function care on oral health status, swallowing ability, and quality of life in stroke survivors.
title: Evaluation Project for Hospital Discharge Planning Bridging Oral Health Care

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to find out whether amivantamab, works better than careful monitoring without additional treatment in participants with unresected locally advanced (L/A) head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) after chemoradiotherapy. HNSCC is a type of cancer that develops in the head and neck regions, including the lining that covers inside of the mouth and throat. The study will measure how long participants remain free from cancer worsening, recurrence, or death.

brief_summary:
This observational study aims to assess and compare body posture in school-aged children who regularly participate in swimming training and children who do not practice swimming. A total of 60 children attending fourth and eighth grades will be included in the study.

Body posture will be assessed using the non-invasive Moiré 4G method, which allows the evaluation of spinal curvature and body asymmetry. Additionally, parents or legal guardians will complete a questionnaire concerning their children's physical activity, swimming training, lifestyle habits, and musculoskeletal health.

The study will investigate differences in postural parameters between swimmers and non-swimmers and examine potential associations between body posture, age, sex, and physical activity levels.
lead_sponsor: Józef Piłsudski University of Physical Education
primary_outcomes: Asymmetry in the Distance of the Inferior Scapular Angles from the Spine (OL)
title: Body Posture Assessment in School-Aged Swimmers and Non-Swimmers Using Moiré 4G

brief_summary:
This study aims to understand how type 2 diabetes and periodontitis (gum disease) are associated with lactate levels in saliva and gene activity in blood immune cells.

The study plans to include 80 adults aged 35 to 70 years, divided into four groups: people without either condition, people with periodontitis only, people with type 2 diabetes only, and people with both conditions.

Participants will provide saliva and blood samples and undergo a dental and gum examination. Researchers will measure lactate, a substance naturally found in saliva, and examine patterns of gene activity in immune cells collected from blood. Blood sugar measurements and gum health findings will also be assessed.

The main goal is to compare saliva lactate levels among the four groups. Researchers will also explore whether saliva lactate levels are related to blood sugar control, gum disease severity, and immune cell activity.

This is an observational study. Participants will not receive any experimental treatment, and the study will not change their usual medical or dental care.
title: Salivary Lactate and Blood Immune Gene Expression in Type 2 Diabetes and Periodontitis

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if eating a bedtime snack helps lower morning fasting blood sugar levels in pregnant patients with gestational diabetes.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does eating a balanced bedtime snack (a snack containing carbohydrates and protein) lower average morning fasting blood sugar levels compared to not eating a bedtime snack?
2. Does eating a bedtime snack reduce the need for diabetes medications (such as insulin or metformin), improve blood sugar levels after meals, or improve health outcomes for the mother and baby?

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of two groups: a bedtime snack group, which will eat a daily bedtime snack containing about 15 grams of carbohydrates and protein for the rest of the pregnancy; or a no bedtime snack group, which will not eat a bedtime snack for the rest of the pregnancy
* Receive standard nutrition counseling and routine prenatal care for gestational diabetes
* Check and record their blood sugar levels daily using a finger-stick or continuous glucose monitor, and keep a food diary
* Attend a follow-up visit 1 week after joining the study, as well as attend regular prenatal clinic visits until delivery to review blood sugar logs and health updates
title: Effects of a Bedtime Snack on Fasting Blood Glucose Levels in Patients With Gestational Diabetes

brief_summary: In-hospital cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) events are usually documented by hand and later transcribed, which can cause timing errors, delays and omissions. This pilot randomized crossover simulation trial compares a hospital-developed emergency auxiliary timing and event recording system with the hospital's current paper resuscitation record. Thirty-six nurses will work in 18 pairs through two 20-minute ACLS simulation scenarios, once with each recording method. The study estimates effects on team clinical performance and documentation accuracy, and explores nurses' experiences through individual interviews.
interventions: Emergency auxiliary timing and event recording system
title: Emergency Auxiliary Timing and Event Recording System During Simulated CPR: A Crossover Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trials is to evaluate whether community health advocacy (CHAMP) and legal assistance (LAW) can work synergistically to reduce violence engagement and improve educational outcomes in middle school aged youth residing in Chicago community areas disproportionately impacted by violence. The main questions it aims to answer are:

How can community health workers (CHWs) screen children and their families for social, education, economic, and health-related needs? How can legal assistance address structural inequities that affect children attending Chicago Public Schools (CPS)? What is the combined impact of CHWs and legal aid wraparound on children and their families?

Researchers will compare the community health worker advocacy intervention (CHAMP) to the combination of community health advocacy and legal aid wraparound intervention (CHAMP-LAW) to see if the combination of community health advocacy and legal aid wraparound can work synergistically to support academic engagement and reduce violence engagement for youth and their families.

Participants will:

* Complete screeners with a CHW in the program
* Receive linkages to care and legal assistance
* Complete up to 5 longitudinal surveys following their enrollment in the program
title: Community Advocates in Mitigating and Preventing Violence With and Without Legal Aid Wraparound

brief_summary:
Every year, over 23,000 people in the U.S. lose a finger, and many of them experience pain and complications, including the formation of painful nerve growths called neuromas. Previous studies show that about 6.6% of people with finger amputations develop painful neuromas, and more than 60% of them need surgery to improve their quality of life.

To prevent neuromas after an amputation, doctors use several techniques, such as cutting the nerve (traction neurectomy) or moving the nerve to a different spot. However, there's no clear "best" method, and research comparing these techniques is limited.

This new study will compare three different methods for preventing neuromas after finger amputations. It will include both traumatic and non-traumatic amputations and will track not just pain, but also issues like cold intolerance and how the injury affects daily activities. The goal is to provide better guidance on how to manage nerve care after finger amputations, ultimately helping both doctors and patients.

This study aims to investigate three different types of surgical methods for the prevention of painful neuroma in digit amputations:

1. Traction neurectomy (TN)
2. Dorsal transposition without coaptation (DT)
3. Dorsal transposition with coaptation (DC)

These three techniques are compared to investigate whether any of them leads to significantly better outcomes regarding pain and cold intolerance in patients undergoing digital amputation.
title: Pain Outcomes After Digital Amputation: A Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing Three Nerve Surgical Techniques

brief_summary: The purpose of this research is to learn whether lack of sleep in people with type 1 diabetes affects blood sugar control, and whether it leads to changes in heart and blood vessel function or memory and thinking ability.

The investigational compound will be administered via oral routes to a cohort of participants presenting with respiratory distress secondary to systemic dehydration or clinical manifestations consistent with asthmatic symptomatology. The primary objective is to establish baseline pharmacological data and safety parameters within this specific patient population.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants with positive Treatment-Related Events
Number of Participants with Negative Treatment-Related Events
title: Assess Efficacy and Safety of Liquid Oxygen: P150-6 in Participants With Difficulty Breathing Caused by Dehydration

brief_summary:
Low back and pelvic pain are common musculoskeletal problems during pregnancy and may interfere with daily activities and quality of life. Pregnancy-related changes in body weight, posture, and spinal mechanics may also affect the activity of the muscles supporting the lower back. A soft lumbosacral orthosis is a supportive device designed to provide support to the lower back and pelvic region. However, its effects on lumbar muscle activity during spinal movements in pregnant women with low back and pelvic pain require further investigation.

The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effectiveness of a soft lumbosacral orthosis on lumbar muscle activity during spinal flexion and extension and on pain intensity in pregnant women with low back and pelvic pain.

A total of 38 pregnant women will participate in this study. Eligible participants will be women younger than 40 years of age, between 20 and 34 weeks of gestation, with a singleton pregnancy and moderate to severe pregnancy-related low back and/or pelvic pain, defined as a score of 50 or higher on a 100-mm Visual Analog Scale (VAS).

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: an intervention group or a control group. Participants in the intervention group will receive a soft lumbosacral orthosis and will be instructed to wear it for 6 hours daily during routine daily activities for 3 weeks. Participants in the control group will continue their usual pregnancy care without receiving the study orthosis.

Assessments will be performed at baseline and after 3 weeks. Lumbar muscle activity will be measured using surface electromyography (sEMG) during spinal flexion and extension. The muscles assessed will include the lumbar erector spinae (longissimus and iliocostalis) and multifidus muscles. Muscle activity will be analyzed using the root mean square (RMS) of the EMG signals. Spinal movement kinematics will also be recorded using a Vicon motion analysis system.

Pain intensity will be assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at baseline and after 3 weeks.

The primary focus of the study is to compare changes in lumbar muscle activity during spinal flexion and extension between the intervention and control groups. Changes in pain intensity will also be evaluated.

Potential adverse effects associated with orthosis use, including skin irritation, discomfort, pressure, sweating, and worsening pain, will be monitored throughout the intervention period.
primary_outcomes: Normalized Lumbar Muscle Activity During Spinal Flexion and Extension
title: Effectiveness of a Soft Lumbosacral Orthosis on Lumbar Muscle Activity During Spinal Flexion and Extension in Pregnant Women With Low Back and Pelvic Pain

brief_summary:
Myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS - Myocardial Injury after Non-Cardiac Surgery) results from myocardial ischemia. It may affect as many as 13-18% of patients during the perioperative period. It manifests as elevated blood troponin levels, although it does not always produce clear clinical symptoms. The risk of premature death and vascular complications is significantly higher in patients who experience perioperative cardiac injury. Approximately 10% of patients with cardiac injury die within 30 days after surgery. The increased risk of premature death persists for up to two years after the cardiac injury.

MINS is defined as myocardial injury that may result in myocardial necrosis due to ischemia. Interruption of blood flow to the myocardium may be associated with thrombosis or reduced perfusion in the setting of increased oxygen demand. This injury must have prognostic significance and occur during or within 30 days after non-cardiac surgery. Based on multivariable analyses in large epidemiological studies, the following diagnostic criteria for MINS have been established: an elevated postoperative troponin level considered to result from myocardial ischemia (with no evidence of a non-ischemic etiology), occurring during or within 30 days after non-cardiac surgery, without the requirement for clinical signs of ischemia (i.e., no subjective symptoms, objective signs, or electrocardiographic changes). These analyses also identified the following perioperative troponin thresholds: (i) low-sensitivity troponin T \>30 ng/L, and (ii) high-sensitivity troponin T (hsTnT) between 20 and \<65 ng/L with an absolute change of at least 5 ng/L-this threshold of change is independently associated with 30-day mortality. Optimal troponin I thresholds for MINS have not been established. For practical purposes, it is recommended to define elevation as any value above the 99th percentile of the reference range for a single troponin I measurement.

The procedures undergone by patients hospitalized in otolaryngology departments are not always "life-saving." They often include surgeries aimed at improving quality of life, eliminating persistent symptoms related, for example, to chronic rhinosinusitis, or improving hearing. Therefore, a thorough analysis of potential procedure-related factors is necessary in order to assess as accurately as possible the probability of cardiovascular complications in each patient. This will enable physicians to make better decisions regarding qualification for surgery and anesthesia, improve patient safety, and help patients make informed decisions about undergoing surgery with full awareness of potential risks and benefits.

The study we are planning would include patients undergoing surgery at the Department and Clinic of Otolaryngology and Laryngological Oncology of the Medical University of Silesia, Faculty of Medical Sciences in Zabrze, Specialist Hospital in Zabrze, as well as at the Fryderyk Chopin University Clinical Hospital in Rzeszów. We plan to include approximately 200 male and female patients over 50 years of age, undergoing surgery under general anesthesia, including endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS), oncological procedures, and microsurgical ear surgery, and classified after anesthesiology consultation as ASA II or III. Only patients who provide informed consent will be included in the study.

Assessment of myocardial injury will be based on analysis of changes in troponin concentration over time. The first measurement will be taken on the day of surgery, at least 2 hours before the procedure begins. Subsequent measurements will be taken 3 hours and 16 to 18 hours after surgery. In total, three blood samples will be collected from each patient, each with a volume of 1 cm³. Patient vital parameters routinely monitored during surgery (blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and end-tidal carbon dioxide levels) will also be analyzed. Before surgery, each patient will undergo echocardiography. Intraoperative blood pressure values will be analyzed in relation to those recorded at hospital admission and those measured twice during the first 6 hours after surgery. A standard component of preoperative preparation for endoscopic sinus surgery is a short course of oral glucocorticosteroid therapy administered for 5 days before surgery, once daily in the morning, at a dose equivalent to 40 mg of prednisone.

Data regarding comorbidities and any abnormalities found on physical examination are collected and archived in a standardized manner during the hospital admission process. Additionally, the health status of each patient included in the study will be assessed using the following measurement tools: the EuroQol Health Questionnaire (EQ-5D-5L), the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), and the Duke Activity Status Index (DASI). In patients undergoing endoscopic sinus surgery, intraoperative bleeding will be assessed using the Boezaart and van der Merwe scale.
primary_outcomes: MINS - Myocardial Injury after Non-cardiac Surgery
title: Assesment of the Clinical Silent Myocardial Injury After ENT Surgeries

brief_summary:
This prospective, multicenter, observational cohort study aims to evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of first-line polatuzumab vedotin plus rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone (Pola-R-CHP) in patients with newly diagnosed high-risk diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), defined by an International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of 3-5.

Approximately 250 patients will be enrolled across participating hospitals in South Korea. The study will include patients treated with Pola-R-CHP as part of routine clinical practice, including older patients and those with comorbidities who may have been underrepresented in previous clinical trials.

The primary objective is to evaluate the 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) rate. Secondary objectives include assessment of treatment response, overall survival, treatment completion, dose modifications, and safety outcomes. Patient-reported symptoms and health-related quality of life will also be assessed.

An exploratory biomarker analysis will be conducted using blood samples collected from patients who provide separate consent.

As this is a non-interventional study, all treatment decisions and clinical assessments will be made by the treating physicians according to routine clinical practice. Participation in the study will not determine or alter the treatment patients receive.

Patients will be followed for 24 months after completion of treatment to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes.
title: Prospective Cohort Study of First-Line Polatuzumab-R-CHP in Newly Diagnosed Large B-Cell Lymphoma

brief_summary:
French Polynesia, a French overseas collectivity in the Pacific Ocean, is home to nearly 279,000 inhabitants living across 76 inhabited islands distributed among five archipelagos. Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) represent a major public health concern in the territory. In 2018, cardiovascular diseases and cancers were the leading causes of death, accounting for 25% and 23% of all mortality, respectively. Although life expectancy remains relatively high, reaching 74.9 years for men and 79.0 years for women in 2022, the burden of chronic diseases continues to grow. This situation is largely driven by the high prevalence of modifiable behavioral and metabolic risk factors within the Polynesian population.

The most recent surveillance survey conducted in 2019 using the World Health Organization (WHO) STEPS methodology revealed alarming results. Approximately 75% of adults in French Polynesia were overweight, including 40% who were classified as obese. The combined impact of unhealthy lifestyles and metabolic risk factors led to an estimated 42% (95% CI: 40-44) of the adult population being at high risk of developing a non-communicable disease. These findings highlight the urgent need for continuous monitoring of NCD risk factors to support evidence-based public health interventions and improve the health system's capacity to respond to current and future challenges.

The STEPS FENUA 2025 survey is part of the ongoing surveillance system for chronic disease risk factors in French Polynesia. Its primary objective is to assess the prevalence of major risk factors associated with non-communicable diseases among the adult population and to better understand health-related behaviors. Specifically, the survey focuses on tobacco use, harmful alcohol consumption, unhealthy dietary habits, physical inactivity, overweight and obesity, hypertension, and selected biological risk markers. The information generated will provide updated and reliable data to guide health promotion strategies, disease prevention programs, and healthcare planning across the territory.

The survey is designed as a cross-sectional epidemiological study based on the standardized WHO STEPS approach, allowing comparisons with previous surveys and international monitoring systems. Data collection is organized into three consecutive stages. The first stage consists of administering a structured questionnaire by trained research interviewers or public health nurses to gather information on sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle behaviors, and NCD risk factors. During the second stage, anthropometric and physical measurements, including weight, height, waist circumference, and blood pressure, are collected by trained personnel. The third stage, conducted between the day of the interview and three days later, involves the collection of biological samples by nurses to assess key metabolic and biochemical indicators.

By providing a comprehensive assessment of behavioral, physical, and biological risk factors, the STEPS FENUA 2025 survey will contribute to a better understanding of the health status of the Polynesian population and strengthen the evidence base needed to develop effective public health policies aimed at reducing the burden of non-communicable diseases in French Polynesia.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of insufficient fruit and vegetable intake
title: Health Behavior and Monitoring of Risk Factors for Non-communicable Diseases in the Population of French Polynesia: STEPS 2025 Survey in French Polynesia

brief_summary:
ItaliVas is a multicenter, observational, retrospective-prospective cohort study designed to characterize the clinical and epidemiological features and long-term outcomes of patients with primary ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) in Italy. AAV comprises three rare systemic vasculitides: granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), microscopic polyangiitis (MPA), and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA).

The study will collect standardized demographic, clinical, laboratory, imaging, histological, and treatment data from patients aged 1 year or older with primary AAV. The retrospective cohort will include patients diagnosed from January 1, 1990, onward, while the prospective cohort will include patients newly diagnosed from study approval through the end of the 10-year enrollment period. Patients will be followed from diagnosis until the last available follow-up, transfer, or death.

The primary objectives are to describe the clinical, laboratory, and therapeutic characteristics of patients with AAV and to evaluate long-term overall and renal survival. Secondary objectives include identifying clinical, laboratory, and treatment-related prognostic factors associated with mortality, progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), and disease relapse; describing organ-specific disease involvement; evaluating relapse rates and treatment response; and assessing cumulative disease-related and treatment-related damage using the Vasculitis Damage Index (VDI).

Approximately 900 patients are expected to be enrolled across specialized Italian centers. Data will be collected longitudinally using standardized electronic case report forms. Survival analyses will be performed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models will be used to identify factors independently associated with long-term outcomes.
title: ItaliVas: Long-Term Outcomes in ANCA-Associated Vasculitis

brief_summary:
Post-mastectomy females commonly experience musculoskeletal complications due to surgical trauma, protective posture, scar-related restriction, shoulder girdle weakness, and altered upper quadrant biomechanics. These changes may lead to rhomboid tightness, myofascial trigger points, forward head posture, neck and shoulder pain, and functional disability. Forward head posture increases mechanical stress on the cervical spine, while rhomboid tightness may further disturb scapular alignment and upper limb function.

This randomized clinical trial will be conducted at Shalamar Hospital, Lahore. A total of 40 post-mastectomy females will be recruited through non-probability convenience sampling and randomly allocated into two groups, with 20 participants in each group. Group A will receive Spray and Stretch Technique, in which vapocoolant spray will be applied over the involved rhomboid muscle followed by gentle stretching.
title: Effects of Spray and Stretch Versus Sustained Pressure Technique in Posture Mastectomy Rhomboid Muscle Tightness Syndrome

brief_summary:
This study aims to learn more about the information that can be obtained directly from measurements through a Nexa cochlear implant during and after surgery. Researchers will investigate whether these measurements can help understand how the implant is interacting with the inner ear and hearing nerve, where the electrodes are positioned inside the cochlea, and potentially how the implant should be programmed and how well a person detects sounds.

The study will also evaluate how well two methods agree in determining the position of the electrode contacts relative to the anatomy of the inner ear and the hearing nerve. One method uses measurements after surgery made through the implant itself. The other uses medical Computed Tomography(CT) imaging made after the surgery. The information collected will also contribute to a clinical research database that may be used to support future research and development. Participants will be told about this potential future use when they provide consent.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical investigation is to compare the Compreflex® adjustable compression medical device with all multi-type compression bandage kits reimbursed in France in patients with venous leg ulcer (VLU). The main question it aims to answer is: Is the adjustable Compreflex® compression device from Sigvaris non inferior to the multi-type bandage kits marketed and reimbursed in France for the treatment of VLU.

Researchers will compare the adjustable Compreflex® compression device to the multi-type bandage kits marketed in France on the complete healing of VLU.

Participants will be randomly allocated to the adjustable Compreflex® compression device or to a multi-type bandage kit, according to the study physican current practice. Then they will be followed-up according to routine patient care, on-site by the study physician and at home by a nurse. Only additional procedures will be added to certain visits:

* Photography of the wound taken by the healthcare providers
* Questionnaires regarding patients quality of life, satisfaction
interventions: Multi-type compression bandage kit ROSIDAL SYS
Multi-type compression bandage kit Biflex Short Strech®

brief_summary: This randomized clinical trial will compare the effects of the Seven Stones Game (Pittu Garam) and the Champ Ball Skills Program on object control skills and eye-hand coordination in school-going children aged 6-10 years. Children who meet the eligibility criteria will be randomly allocated to either the Seven Stones Game group or the Champ Ball Skills Program group. Both interventions will be conducted three times a week for eight weeks with comparable session duration and standardized warm-up and cool-down activities. Object control skills, eye-hand coordination, manual dexterity, and visual-motor integration will be assessed before and after the intervention using standardized assessment tools. The study aims to determine whether a culturally familiar traditional game can provide comparable or different benefits to a structured ball skills program for improving motor performance in school-aged children.
primary_outcomes: The Test of Gross Motor Development-2 (TGMD-2)
title: Comparison of Seven Stone Games and Champ Ball Skills Program

brief_summary:
This study aims to determine whether hybrid telemedical care is as effective as traditional in-person care for adults with diabetic retinopathy, and whether assistance from a patient care navigator improves access to eye care.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups: (1) hybrid telemedicine visits with care navigation, (2) hybrid telemedicine visits without care navigation, (3) in-person visits with care navigation, or (4) in-person visits without care navigation.

Hybrid telemedical care involves eye testing at a nearby site followed by a video or telephone consultation with an eye care provider. Participants assigned to care navigation will receive assistance with scheduling appointments, addressing transportation barriers, accessing community resources, and using telemedicine technology.

Participants will be followed for approximately three years. The study will compare changes in vision, progression of diabetic retinopathy, vision-related quality of life, patient satisfaction, and access to eye care across the study groups.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Best-Corrected Visual Acuity (BCVA)
title: Comparing Hybrid Telemedical Care With Standard In-person Care for Diabetic Eye Disease

brief_summary:
This study examines how physicians use advice from a large language model when deciding whether to start blood pressure medication. The study team plans to enroll 15 to 20 licensed physicians who care for adults with hypertension in China, including at least five from each of three hospital levels. Each physician will complete two rounds of online case review in one session lasting about one hour.

In the first round, physicians will independently decide whether to start blood pressure medication for 30 cases. They can consult a guideline summary and a cardiovascular risk calculator. In the second round, they will review the same cases in a different order. The platform will show their earlier decision and a previously generated AI recommendation for each case.

The main analysis will focus on cases with blood pressure below 130/80 mm Hg and at least one high-risk feature. Among the cases judged correctly in the first round, the study will compare how often decisions change to incorrect medication initiation in cases with incorrect versus correct AI advice.

The cases use publicly available, de-identified data from the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. The decisions are recorded for research and have no role in patient care.
interventions: Display of a Large Language Model Recommendation
primary_outcomes: Difference in New Errors Between Cases With Incorrect and Correct AI Recommendations
title: How AI Advice Influences Physicians' Decisions to Start Blood Pressure Medication

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial was to learn whether a human-equivalent lactoferrin supplement (effera) taken with a low dose of iron can improve iron status and hair health in adult women with low iron stores (low ferritin). Lactoferrin is a protein found naturally in human milk and other body fluids that helps the body manage iron.

The main questions it aimed to answer were:

* Does taking effera with iron for 6 weeks raise ferritin (a blood marker of the body's iron stores)?
* Does it change other blood markers of iron status, red blood cells, or inflammation?
* Does it reduce hair shedding, measured with an at-home hair pull test?
* Does it change how participants rate their energy, fatigue, mood, hair health, and skin health?

Researchers compared two doses of effera (100 mg per day or 50 mg per day, each taken with 5 mg of iron) to see whether the higher dose works better. Neither participants nor researchers knew which dose a participant was taking. There was no placebo group.

Participants:

* Took their assigned supplement every day for 6 weeks
* Had fasting blood drawn by a mobile phlebotomist at the start of the study and after 2, 4, and 6 weeks
* Completed an online questionnaire about energy, fatigue, mood, hair, and skin each week
* Did a simple hair pull test at home each week and counted the hairs that came out
* Reported any side effects to the study team

The study was fully remote. The supplement was shipped to participants' homes, and consent, questionnaires, and communication took place online.
primary_outcomes: Change in Hair Shedding Measured by Modified Hair Pull Test
title: Human Lactoferrin (Effera) Plus Iron for Iron Status and Hair Health in Active Women

brief_summary: The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to determine to compare the effects of the McKenzie Method and Mulligan mobilization with suboccipital inhibition in reducing pain and disability and improving cervical range of motion in patients with cervicogenic headache. Participants were allocated into two groups randomly, with Group A receiving the McKenzie Method + Suboccipital Muscle Inhibition and the other Group B receiving Mulligan C1-C2 Rotational SNAG + McKenzie Method + Suboccipital Muscle Inhibition. Both groups received 30-40-minute sessions three times weekly for four weeks. The Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), Neck Disability Index (NDI), Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6), and cervical range of motion flexion-rotation test, were assessed at baseline, week 2, and week 4. The findings of this study may help determine the more effective intervention for improving symptoms and functional outcomes in patients with cervicogenic headache.
interventions: Active Comparator: McKenzie Method + suboccipital muscle inhibition
Experimental: Mulligan Mobilization (SNAGs) + McKenzie Method (MDT) +Suboccipital Inhibition (SMI).
title: Comparative Effects of Mackenzie and Mulligan Mobilization With Suboccipital Inhibition in Cervicogenic Headache

brief_summary: Impact of Colloid versus Crystalloid Perioperative Fluid Therapy on Venous Congestion and Clinical Outcomes Assessed by VExUS in Major Orthopedic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
interventions: Perioperative fluids provided exclusively as balanced crystalloids in 500-1000 mL boluses to maintain hemodynamic targets.

title: Impact of Colloid Versus Crystalloid Perioperative Fluid Therapy on Venous Congestion and Clinical Outcomes Assessed by VExUS in Major Orthopedic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

brief_summary:
Chronic low back pain, defined as pain in the lumbar region persisting for more than three months, is the leading cause of disability worldwide. A specific form of low back pain, characterized by vertebral endplate changes (known as Modic type 1 changes) and prolonged inflammatory pain, affects a subset of the population and is associated with active discopathy.

Current treatments are generally invasive and have limited efficacy (e.g., intradiscal injections, bracing). Auricular vagus nerve stimulation using electrical impulses delivered through an earbud-like device, such as Vagustim, is an innovative, clinically recognized, approved, and effective approach to restoring balance in parasympathetic nervous system dysfunction. However, no randomized controlled trial has yet evaluated its efficacy in chronic low back pain.

The aim of this study is therefore to conduct a comparative trial of auricular vagus nerve stimulation (experimental treatment) versus sham treatment, with the objective of improving pain management in chronic low back pain through a novel, non-invasive, and easy-to-use therapeutic approach.

We hypothesize that auricular vagus nerve stimulation has a clinically significant effect on low back pain intensity in patients with active discopathy.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of patients with a 30% reduction in the levelof LBP intensity (in the previous 48h) measured on a visual analog scale (VAS) at 1 month.
title: Effect of Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Lumbar Active Discopathy

brief_summary:
Carpal tunnel syndrome is a common condition caused by compression of the median nerve at the wrist. Endoscopic carpal tunnel release (ECTR) is a commonly performed surgical procedure used to relieve this compression. During ECTR, some surgeons also release the antebrachial fascia, while others do not. It is currently unclear whether release of the antebrachial fascia provides additional benefit when performed during routine ECTR.

The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to compare clinical and functional outcomes following ECTR with release of the antebrachial fascia versus ECTR without release of the antebrachial fascia. Participants undergoing ECTR will be randomly assigned to one of the two surgical approaches and followed for approximately 6 weeks after surgery. Study outcomes will include patient-reported outcome measures, clinical assessments, and complications to determine whether antebrachial fascia release affects recovery and postoperative outcomes.
interventions: Antebrachial Fascia Release During Endoscopic Carpal Tunnel Release
Endoscopic Carpal Tunnel Release Without Antebrachial Fascia Release
title: Antebrachial Fascia Release During Endoscopic Carpal Tunnel Release

brief_summary: This phase IIa, multicenter, randomized, open-label, controlled trial with blinded endpoint assessment will evaluate the preliminary efficacy and safety of anisodine hydrobromide in patients with acute vertebrobasilar artery occlusion undergoing endovascular treatment.
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University
title: Anisodine Hydrobromide in Patients With Acute Vertebrobasilar Artery Occlusion Undergoing Endovascular Treatment

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of multiple doses of HB0043 in healthy adult participants.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of subjects with drug related adverse events (AEs)
title: Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetic Characteristics of HB0043 in Healthy Adult Participants

brief_summary: The use of psychoactive substances (tobacco, alcohol, cannabis) is widespread in France. Dentists, as primary care providers, are particularly well-positioned to implement screening and brief intervention (SBI). However, there are no data on their practices. This multicenter project (Brest, Tours) consists of two phases: 1) a mixed-methods assessment of screening and brief intervention practices among dentists in private practice in France (a qualitative study using semi-structured interviews, followed by a national online survey), 2) the development of a training program dedicated to screening and brief intervention through a Delphi consensus, a pilot feasibility study, and a randomized controlled trial comparing trained dentists with dentists practicing according to their usual practices. No patients are included. Only volunteer dentists participate in this project.
primary_outcomes: Number of psychoactive substance use screenings performed by dentists
title: Screening and Brief Intervention for Psychoactive Substance Use by Dentists in France

brief_summary:
This study is for patients who have a type of blood cancer called acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that has come back or has not gone away after standard treatments. The study will test a new kind of treatment made from a patient's own white blood cells, called BiCAR T cells.

T cells are special infection-fighting cells in the immune system. In this study, the patient's T cells are collected from their blood and changed in the laboratory to recognize and attack AML cells. The modified cells, called BiCAR T cells, have been given two "receptors" that help them find and destroy cancer cells in two ways - one that recognizes a target called CLL-1, and another that recognizes CD70, a protein found on many leukemia cells.

This "two-target" approach is designed to help the T cells find more cancer cells and stay active longer in the body. After the T cells are changed in the lab, they are given back to the patient through an IV.

Before receiving the BiCAR T cells, patients will get a short course of lymphodepleting chemotherapy. This step, called lymphodepletion, helps make space in the body for the new T cells to grow and work more effectively.

The main goals of this study are to:

1. Find the safest and most effective dose of BiCAR T cells;
2. Learn about possible side effects; and
3. See how the treatment affects leukemia cells in the blood and bone marrow.
conditions: Relapsed or Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
interventions: Autologous BiCAR T cells targeting CLL-1 and CD70
primary_outcomes: Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD) of BiCAR T-cells
title: CD70/CLL-1.BiCAR T Cells for Relapsed or Refractory AML

brief_summary:
Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a mood disorder that causes a continued feeling of sadness and loss of interest. It is a common and serious illness that can cause both emotional and physical symptoms such as feelings of sadness, irritability, not being able to focus on activities, tiredness, changes in eating habits, and aches and pains. The study aims to measure any changes in depression symptoms and the assessment of adverse events of AGN-151607-DP compared to placebo in participants with MDD.

AGN-151607-DP is an investigational drug being developed for treatment of moderate to severe MDD in adults. This study has a double-blind treatment period (DBTP) and an open-label treatment period (OLTP). In the DBTP, participants will be randomly placed in treatment groups to receive either AGN-151607-DP or matching placebo. In the OLTP, participants who are eligible to continue will receive AGN-151607-DP. Around 378 adult participants will be enrolled in the study at approximately 47 sites worldwide. The total study duration is approximately 28 weeks.

There may be higher treatment burden for participants in this trial compared to their standard of care (due to study procedures). Participants will attend regular bi-weekly or monthly visits during the study. The effects of the treatment will be checked by medical assessments, blood tests, checking for side effects and completing questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) Total Score
Number of Participants with Adverse Events (AEs)
title: A Study to Assess the Change in Disease Activity and Adverse Events of AGN-151607-DP for the Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder in Adult Participants

brief_summary: This is a two-center retrospective observational cohort study of patients with colorectal cancer who underwent curative-intent surgery and had at least one pathologically confirmed tumor deposit. Existing clinical records and H\&E whole-slide images of tumor deposits will be used to develop a patient-level prognostic score integrating tumor deposit morphology and pathomic features, local tertiary lymphoid structure features, and routine clinicopathological information. The model will be evaluated in an independent external-center cohort. The primary outcome is postoperative disease-free survival; overall survival is a secondary outcome. Selected archived tissue may undergo multiplex immunofluorescence for exploratory interpretation. The study does not assign treatment or alter clinical care.
lead_sponsor: Sixth Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University
title: Tumor Deposit Pathology and Prognostic Risk in Colorectal Cancer
