title: A Study of [177Lu]Lu-XT381 in Participants With PSMA-Positive Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate how accurately a breath test can detect 10 types of cancer and suggest which type of cancer a person may have. The test measures chemicals called volatile organic compounds in the air people breathe out. Researchers will compare the breath test results with diagnoses established through standard medical care.

The study plans to enroll 1,000 adults at several hospitals, including people with cancer, people with related noncancerous conditions, and healthy volunteers. Participants will provide a breath sample and allow the study team to review relevant medical records. For participants without cancer, the team will check medical records or contact them about 3 months after sampling and, if needed, again at about 6 months. Breath test results will be used for research, and participants will continue to receive their usual medical care.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University
title: A Study of a Breath Test to Detect Different Types of Cancer and Identify Where They Start

brief_summary: Pilot clinical trial of Rasburicase administration in neonatal patients with acute renal injury with hyperuricemia
primary_outcomes: Rate of participants with renal function improvement
title: Rasburicase in Hyperuricemic Neonates With Acute Kidney Injury

brief_summary: Cervical spondylotic radiculopathy (CSR) causes neck-shoulder pain and upper-limb radiating numbness due to nerve-root compression, severely impairing quality of life. Acupuncture is recommended for pain management, yet clinical acupoint selection mostly relies on personal experience without objective biomarkers, leading to variable treatment responses. High-density electroencephalography (HD-EEG) can non-invasively record brain neuronal oscillations related to pain perception. This single-center, prospective, participant-blinded randomized controlled trial will enroll 120 CSR patients stratified by MRI-measured nerve-root compression (mild \<3 mm; moderate 3-5 mm; severe \>5 mm). Participants in each stratum will be randomly assigned 1:1 to either Meridian-based Acupuncture group or Cervical Jiaji Acupuncture group. All participants will receive 3 sessions per week for 2 weeks. Clinical assessments (VAS pain score, Neck Disability Index) and 64-channel HD-EEG resting-state recordings will be collected at baseline, 2-week post-treatment, and 1-month follow-up. The primary objectives are to compare pain relief between two acupoint schemes and identify pain-related EEG oscillatory biomarkers. This study intends to build a "compression severity-EEG-optimal acupoint" matching standard, provide neurophysiological evidence for acupoint specificity, and support personalized acupuncture decision-making for CSR patients.
primary_outcomes: Change in Visual Analog Scale (VAS) Pain Score
Changes of Key-region High-density EEG Oscillatory Features
title: Acupuncture Point Matching for Cervical Spondylotic Radiculopathy With Different Nerve-Root Compression Grades Using High-Density EEG Neuro-Oscillations

brief_summary:
Critically ill patients lose muscle mass rapidly during their intensive care unit (ICU) stay, which contributes to prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer hospital stays and lasting functional limitations. Nutrition therapy and early mobilization each help, but they have mostly been tested separately and only during the ICU stay.

The SYNERGY trial tests whether combining personalized nutrition, guided by indirect calorimetry, with early mobilization improves quality of life 6 months later in adults who need mechanical ventilation. The combined program continues after ICU discharge, up to day 28 or hospital discharge.

A total of 224 adults in four Swiss ICUs will be randomly assigned (1:1) to the combined program or to standard nutrition and physiotherapy care. The main outcome is quality of life measured with the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire at 6 months. Other outcomes include muscle mass and function, physical recovery, inflammation, gut microbiota, survival, length of stay, infections, and functional, mental and cognitive health at 6 months.
primary_outcomes: Health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5L index score)
title: Personalized Nutrition and Early Mobilization in Mechanically Ventilated ICU Patients (SYNERGY)

brief_summary:
The main purpose of this study is to measure how much tersolisib gets into the bloodstream and how long it takes the body to eliminate it in participants with liver impairment compared to participants with normal liver function. The safety of tersolisib will also be evaluated.

For each participant, the study will last about 7 weeks including a 14-night stay in the Clinical Research Unit (CRU) and one follow-up telephone call.
lead_sponsor: Scorpion Therapeutics, a wholly owned subsidiary of Eli Lilly and Company
primary_outcomes: PK: Area Under the Concentration Versus Time Curve (AUC) of Tersolisib
title: A Study of Tersolisib (LY4064809) in Participants With Liver Impairment Compared With Participants With Normal Liver Impairment.

brief_summary:
Venous leg ulcers (VLUs) represent an advanced manifestation of chronic venous disease and are associated with prolonged healing, frequent recurrence, impaired quality of life, and substantial healthcare costs. Despite advances in compression therapy, wound management, and venous interventions, standardized prospective data regarding the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes of patients with VLUs in Mexico remain limited.

The National Multicenter Prospective Registry of Venous Ulcers of the Lower Limbs (RENUVI-Mexico) is a nationwide, prospective, observational, longitudinal cohort study designed to characterize patients with active VLUs, evaluate real-world treatment strategies, identify factors associated with healing and recurrence, and assess healthcare utilization and disparities in access to care.

The registry aims to enroll 2,000 adults with active lower-extremity ulcers of confirmed or predominantly venous etiology from public and private healthcare institutions throughout Mexico. Participants will undergo standardized baseline assessment, including demographics, comorbidities, ulcer characteristics, CEAP classification, Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS), vascular evaluation, and treatment documentation.

The primary outcome is complete healing of the index ulcer at 24 weeks, defined as 100% epithelialization, absence of drainage, and no further requirement for wound dressings. Secondary outcomes include time to healing, wound-area reduction, healing at 12 and 52 weeks, ulcer recurrence, pain, quality of life, treatment adherence, complications, venous interventions, and healthcare resource utilization.

Participants will be evaluated at baseline and weeks 4, 12, 24, and 52. Treatment will follow routine clinical practice without protocol-mandated interventions. Data will be collected through a secure electronic platform and analyzed using descriptive statistics, survival analysis, and multivariable models.

RENUVI-Mexico aims to generate national real-world evidence to improve venous ulcer management, identify healthcare disparities, support quality improvement initiatives, and guide future multicenter research and healthcare planning in Mexico.
title: Mexico National Registry of Venous Leg Ulcers

brief_summary:
This study is about women in Australia who are in menopause. They had symptoms including hot flashes and night sweats (also known as vasomotor symptoms or VMS). Their own doctor had prescribed them fezolinetant for hot flashes and night sweats, as part of their routine health care.

This study is about collecting information only. The women's own doctor decided on treatment, not the study sponsor (Astellas).

In this study, medical records will be reviewed from women who have been prescribed fezolinetant in Australia. Information will be collected just before and up to 6 months after the women started taking fezolinetant.

Researchers will check if the women's sleep improved after taking fezolinetant. They will also learn if the women had fewer or less severe hot flashes, as well as about the women's wellbeing, and treatment satisfaction. Safety information will also be collected.
primary_outcomes: The percentage of women reporting improvement in sleep disturbance: Patient global impression of change Sleep Disturbance (PGI-C SD)
title: A Study to Learn About Sleep Outcomes of Women in Menopause Taking Fezolinetant in Clinical Practice in Australia

brief_summary:
Background: Parent-infant bonding is conceptualized as a parent-driven process that begins with the intention to have a child and can continue to evolve over time. Perinatal mental illness encompasses psychiatric disorders occurring during pregnancy and up to one year postpartum and may adversely affect mother-infant bonding. Grupo de Vínculo Madre-Bebé is a structured group-based intervention designed for women with perinatal mental disorders and infants aged six months or younger, with the aim of enhancing mother-infant bonding. This study describes the protocol developed to evaluate the effectiveness and implementation of a Matter-Bonding Group Intervention in the Portuguese context, adapted from the original mother-baby bonding group.

Methods: This is a hybrid effectiveness-implementation study of the mother-baby bonding group delivered at the Department of Psychiatry and Mental Health of the hospital unit, integrated within the Perinatal Mental Health Program of the Department of a hospital unit located in a rural region of Portugal.

Conclusion: The Matter-Bonding Group Intervention is anticipated to be acceptable, appropriate, feasible and effective in reducing mental health symptoms, improving mother-infant bonding, and functioning (sleep, marital relationship). The study is expected to identify barriers and facilitators to its implementation that can inform tailored implementation strategies, optimize intervention delivery, and enhance its adoption, sustainability, and effectiveness in perinatal mental health settings.
primary_outcomes: Longitudinal Change in Depressive Symptoms Assessed by the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)
Longitudinal Change in State Anxiety Assessed by the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI-S)
Longitudinal Change in Mother-Infant Bonding Assessed by the Postpartum Bonding Questionnaire (PBQ)
Longitudinal Change in the Brief Symptom Inventory (BSI)
title: Matter-Bonding Group Intervention in the Context of Perinatal Mental Illness

brief_summary:
Background:

Cooking at home is a good way for a person to eat a healthy diet. Some people enjoy cooking, whereas others find it stressful. Researchers want to know more about how brain activity affects emotional and physical responses when people cook.

Objective:

To learn how the brain works when people cook.

Eligibility:

People aged 25 to 55 years who are right handed. Both professional cooks and people who cook only at home are needed.

Design:

Participants will have 3 or 4 clinic visits.

Day 1: They will give samples of blood, saliva, and a tongue brushing. They will report everything they ate over the past 24 hours. They will have a functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) scan: They will watch videos of cooking and other activities during the scan.

Day 2: They will cook a dish they know well 4 times. During each cooking event, 2 of these conditions will occur:

Either (1) they will wear a cap with sensors to measure electrical activity in the brain (EEG) or (2) they will wear different devices to monitor heart rate, sweat glands, eye movements, and other measures of stress. Also, either (1) they will cook their dish in their usual way or (2) they will follow instructions from the study team.

Day 3: They will cook their dish 2 times, while wearing the EEG and the other monitoring devices at the same time. They will cook once their own way, and once following instructions.

Day 4 is optional. Participants will drink a breakfast shake, then have some physical and memory tests. Then they will select portion sizes of food they would like to eat.
lead_sponsor: National Institutes of Health Clinical Center (CC)
title: Biobehavioral Investigations on Cooking: Measuring Biobehavioral and Neural Measurements in Cooking

brief_summary: Post-dural puncture headache (PDPH) is one of the most common complications of spinal anesthesia, and women undergoing cesarean delivery are at particular risk. The optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD), measured noninvasively by ultrasound, reflects changes in intracranial pressure because the subarachnoid space surrounding the optic nerve is continuous with the intracranial subarachnoid space. This prospective, single-center, observational study aims to evaluate the perioperative change in ONSD in women undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia and to investigate whether this change is associated with the development of PDPH. The study does not alter routine anesthetic or surgical care; the only study-specific procedure is noninvasive ultrasound measurement of the ONSD at predefined perioperative time points, followed by systematic assessment for PDPH.
primary_outcomes: Perioperative change in optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD)
Association between perioperative ONSD change and post-dural puncture headache (PDPH)
title: Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter Changes After Spinal Anesthesia for Cesarean Delivery

brief_summary:
Background: Periorbital hyperpigmentation (POH) is a common condition caused by various endogenous and exogenous factors. It has multiple therapeutic modalities, including topical agents, chemical peeling, lasers, fillers, and microneedling (MN), which has a significant role in treatment of POH. Tranexamic Acid (TXA) with microneedling was used in treatment of melasma showing promising results. Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) is used for peeling. It causes mild skin erythema for 2-3 days and light exfoliation at 3-5 days.

The aim of the study: It was to compare the efficacy and safety of MN with TXA versus MN with TCA 10 % for treatment of POH.

Patients and methods: This was a prospective split face clinical trial which included 31 patients with POH. The study patients were subjected to full history taking, clinical examination including clinical assessment of POH degree, and dermoscopic examination before and after treatment. Both treatment regiments were applied, MN with TXA on the right side and MN with TCA 10 % on the left side.
title: Microneedling With Tranexamic Acid or Trichloroacetic Acid 10 % in Treatment of Periorbital Hyperpigmentation

brief_summary:
This is a prospective observational study involving approximately 50 patients with advanced lung cancer at Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology.

The purpose of this study is to investigate the relationship between molecular characteristics, tumor immune microenvironment, treatment response, disease progression, and survival in patients with advanced lung cancer, with a particular focus on targeted therapy and immunotherapy.

The study will not change patients' routine medical care or treatment plans, and no additional biopsies or invasive procedures will be performed for research purposes. After routine pathological examination, immunohistochemistry, and clinically necessary molecular testing have been completed, any remaining tumor tissue may be used for research only with the participant's informed consent.

Depending on tissue availability, quality, and testing conditions, the remaining tumor tissue will undergo bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and other relevant molecular analyses.

Clinical, pathological, imaging, treatment, and follow-up information will also be collected. Treatment response will be evaluated, and progression-free survival and overall survival will be assessed during follow-up.

By integrating clinical information with molecular and immune microenvironment data, this study aims to identify potential biomarkers associated with treatment response and prognosis in advanced lung cancer.
lead_sponsor: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
title: Prospective Multi-omics Study in Advanced Lung Cancer

brief_summary: Evaluate the feasibility of using the Axoft Diana Connect System for up to 30 day use.
conditions: Feasibility of Safe Insertion and Sub Chronic Neural Recording With a Diana Connect Device
title: Feasibility Trial Using a Novel Depth Electrode Subchronic System in Subjects With DoC

brief_summary: The objective of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the efficacy and feasibility of perturbation-based balance training (PBT) for improving reactive balance and preventing falls in people with Parkinson's Disease (PwPD). Participants will be randomly allocated to either an intervention group, undergoing treadmill-based PBT, or an active control group, performing conventional treadmill training without additional perturbations (CTT). Both groups will receive 12 training sessions within 4 to 6 weeks and will undergo assessments at baseline, post-intervention and 6-month follow-up. The primary outcome is reactive balance in response to perturbations during treadmill walking. Key secondary outcome is reactive balance in response to perturbations during standing. Further secondary outcomes include real-life falls, feasibility and acceptability of the intervention, balance and gait performance, concerns about falling and balance confidence, and disease-related motor symptoms.
primary_outcomes: Reactive balance performance in response to gait perturbations post intervention - modified Dynamic Stepping Threshold Test (mDSTT)
title: Perturbation Training for Reactive Balance in People With Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary: Electrolytes, such as sodium and potassium, are minerals found in many beverages. Drinks that contain electrolytes may help the body retain more of the fluid that is consumed. Most previous research on these types of beverages has been conducted in athletes during or after exercise, when people are already dehydrated. Less is known about how these beverages affect hydration during typical daily activities that involve mostly sitting with occasional light walking. This study will compare two flavored waters containing electrolytes with plain water to determine their effects on hydration in healthy women.
interventions: Flavored, sweetened water with electrolytes containing less sodium
Flavored, sweetened water with electrolytes containing more sodium
title: A Randomized Trial to Determine the Effect of Flavored, Sweetened Water With Electrolytes on Fluid Balance in Women

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate the effect of a structured 4-week prenatal yoga intervention on maternal-fetal attachment and maternal self-efficacy among pregnant women in Sleman Regency, Indonesia. Utilizing a quasi-experimental design with non-equivalent control and intervention groups across community health centers, the study compares the outcomes of participants receiving prenatal yoga alongside routine antenatal care versus those receiving routine antenatal care alone.
title: Impact of Prenatal Yoga on Maternal-Fetal Attachment and Self-Efficacy Among Indonesian Pregnant Women

brief_summary: This is a phase II, randomized, sham controlled, clinical trial. This clinical trial has as primary objective to evaluate changes in EEG of a Trigeminal Nerve Stimulation (TNS) treatment protocol for patients with moderate / severe depressive episode
title: EEG Changes Related to TNS

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational registry is to determine how well ThermoCore controls body temperature in adults whose doctors have determined they need temperature management. ThermoCore is an FDA-cleared tube that is placed through the nose into the stomach. It connects to a temperature-control machine to cool or warm the patient from inside the body, and it can also drain the stomach or deliver fluids, like a standard nasogastric tube.

The main questions this registry aims to answer are: - How quickly does ThermoCore bring a patient's temperature to the target the doctor chose? - How well does ThermoCore keep the temperature at that target? - How often do patients shiver during treatment? - Which temperature-control approaches and medical conditions do doctors use ThermoCore for? - How easy do doctors and nurses find ThermoCore to place and use?

The treating doctor decides, on their own, whether a patient needs temperature control and whether to use ThermoCore. Being in the registry does not change the patient's care, and there are no extra tests, procedures, or visits. Researchers will collect information that is already recorded in the medical record while ThermoCore is in use (up to 72 hours), such as temperature readings, shivering scores, and any device problems. The clinician who placed or operated the device will also complete a short questionnaire about their experience after ThermoCore is removed.
title: ThermoCore Post-Market Registry

brief_summary: This prospective multicenter study will evaluate adults with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) who are newly prescribed standard-of-care inhaled treprostinil. Hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI will be performed before treatment and after 12 weeks to assess changes in lung gas transfer, including red blood cell (RBC) defect percentage. At 12 weeks, MRI will also be performed before and after a dose of inhaled treprostinil to characterize acute effects. The study will examine whether changes in 129Xe MRI measures are associated with treatment response, including changes in six-minute walk distance, pulmonary function, and plasma BNP levels.
conditions: Pulmonary Hypertension Associated With Interstitial Lung Disease
primary_outcomes: Change in 129Xe MRI RBC gas transfer defect percentage
title: Inhaled Treprostinil Response Assessed by Hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI in Adults With Pulmonary Hypertension Associated With Interstitial Lung Disease (X-TRIPP)

brief_summary: The investigator and research team plan to evaluate the impact of an informational website, WellPrept and its "Journey" web-based tool on patient education during the postoperative period following their HoLEP and/or kidney stone removal procedure.
primary_outcomes: Characterized types of questions and concerns that prompt additional postoperative healthcare utilization following HoLEP and or kidney stone removal procedures.
title: Utilization of WellPrept Journey for Postoperative Education and Patient Satisfaction Following HoLEP and Kidney Stone Surgery

brief_summary: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) elastography is a non-invasive method for evaluating tissue stiffness. Strain elastography has been studied in chronic pancreatitis, but no data exist for two-dimensional shear wave elastography performed during EUS (2D EUS-SWE). This prospective single-center pilot study evaluates whether pancreatic parenchymal stiffness measured by 2D EUS-SWE differs between patients with chronic pancreatitis and patients with a normal pancreas, and how SWE values relate to the Rosemont classification (consistent, suggestive, or indeterminate for chronic pancreatitis).
interventions: Diagnostic Test: 2D EUS shear wave elastography
lead_sponsor: Institutul Regional de Gastroenterologie & Hepatologie Prof. dr. Octavian Fodor
title: Endoscopic Ultrasound Shear Wave Elastography for the Diagnosis of Chronic Pancreatitis

brief_summary:
This study investigated whether performing physical activity before a lecture could improve learning outcomes in undergraduate physiotherapy students. Specifically, it compared two different exercise approaches: brief exercise snacks and a longer session of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise.

A total of 69 undergraduate physiotherapy students participated in this randomized controlled trial and were equally assigned to three groups. The Exercise Snacks group performed three 1-minute bouts of vigorous physical activity, including stair climbing, bodyweight squats, and high-knee running or marching, at approximately 30-minute intervals before the lecture. The Exercise Priming group completed 30 minutes of moderate-intensity cycling before the lecture. The control group remained seated without performing structured physical activity before the lecture.

All participants attended the same standardized lecture on exercise prescription in cardiopulmonary rehabilitation. Learning outcomes were evaluated using knowledge tests administered before the lecture, immediately after the lecture, and seven days later. Additional assessments examined students' perceived mental effort during learning, confidence in their physiotherapy knowledge and skills, and ability to apply what they had learned to practical clinical scenarios.

The study aimed to determine whether brief exercise snacks and longer aerobic exercise sessions could improve knowledge acquisition, short-term knowledge retention, learning-related mental effort, self-confidence, and practical clinical performance compared with a sedentary control condition. The findings may help identify practical ways to incorporate physical activity into university teaching schedules.
title: Effects of Pre-Lecture Exercise on Learning in Physiotherapy Students

brief_summary:
This study compares two materials used to make rigid gas-permeable contact lenses, a type of hard lens that allows oxygen to pass through to the eye. The materials are ONE-X, a new material being studied, and Boston XO, a material already used in contact lenses. Both sets of lenses have the same Elipsys STD design. The study aims to find out how comfortable the lenses are at the end of the day, how well they work, and whether they cause any eye problems during wear.

The study plans to enroll 24 adults in Bilbao, Spain. Each participant will wear both types of lenses in both eyes, one type at a time. The order will be assigned at random. Participants will wear each type for 30 days, with a two-day break between periods when they will not wear either set of study lenses. Participants and the clinicians assessing the study outcomes will not know which material is being worn during each period.

The main measure is how comfortable the lenses feel at the end of the day after 30 days of wearing each type. Participants will rate their comfort on a scale from 1 to 10, with higher scores indicating greater comfort. The study team will also check vision, lens fit, and eye health, and will record any symptoms or adverse events.
conditions: Performance of Rigid Gas-Permeable Contact Lenses
interventions: Elipsys STD Contact Lenses Made From ONE-X
Elipsys STD Contact Lenses Made From Boston XO
title: Clinical Evaluation of ONE-X Versus Boston XO Rigid Gas-Permeable Contact Lenses

brief_summary:
This study tests ETHOS, an online mindfulness program for hospital practitioners. ETHOS combines mindfulness training with a short reflection on morally difficult situations at work.

The main questions are:

* Do enough practitioners enroll and stay in the study?
* Do participants complete the modules and practice between sessions?
* Are participants satisfied with the program?

The study also describes changes in emotional exhaustion, well-being, stress and moral distress over 18 weeks. This first study is not designed to show whether the program works.

About 30 practitioners from one hospital in France will take part. Adult practitioners involved in patient care can take part, for example physicians, nurses and allied health professionals. All participants will receive the program. There is no comparison group.

Participants will:

* Follow one online module each week for six weeks (about one hour per week)
* Follow a booster module at week 10
* Be invited to do a guided practice of 5 or 10 minutes each day
* Fill in questionnaires before the program and at weeks 6, 10 and 18

Researchers will also interview 10 to 12 participants about their experience of the program.
primary_outcomes: Time to reach the target sample
Use of micro-practices and of the four-step tool
title: An Ethics-Informed Online Mindfulness Program for Hospital Practitioners

brief_summary:
Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is one of the most common chronic complications of diabetes mellitus. The main symptoms of DPN include numbness, pain, paresthesia, and burning sensations in the extremities, which can significantly affect patients' quality of life. Pharmacological treatments for DPN are associated with uncertain therapeutic benefits, potential side effects, and high costs. Previous clinical studies have reported that low-level laser therapy (LLLT) may relieve clinical symptoms and improve nerve function. However, studies investigating the effects of high-intensity laser therapy (HILT), which promotes tissue repair through its biostimulatory effects, on the symptoms of DPN remain limited.

The aim of this study is to investigate the clinical effectiveness of high-intensity laser therapy combined with exercise on pain, pain coping strategies, functional mobility, and quality of life in patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
primary_outcomes: Change in Pain Assessed by the McGill Pain Questionnaire
Change in Neuropathy Symptoms and Signs Assessed by the Michigan Neuropathy Screening Instrument (MNSI)

Change in Pain Coping Strategies Assessed by the Pain Coping Inventory (PCI)
title: Effectiveness of High-Intensity Laser Therapy in Patients With Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy : Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this pragmatic randomized controlled trial is to determine whether an enhanced Community Health Worker (CHW) model (T2D-CATCH) that combines continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) education and support with health-related social needs (HRSN) navigation can improve diabetes control in adults ages 18-75 with high-risk type 2 diabetes (T2D) in the Bronx, NY. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does participation in the T2D-CATCH intervention result in a greater reduction in Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) at 6 months compared with usual medical and social care?
* Does the T2D-CATCH intervention increase uptake and continued use of CGM and improve HRSN resolution?
* Does the T2D-CATCH intervention improve diabetes-related distress, diabetes self-management behaviors, and patient experience?
* Can the T2D-CATCH intervention be successfully implemented across multiple primary care sites, as measured by reach, acceptability, feasibility, adoption, implementation fidelity, and cost?

Researchers will compare participants randomized to the T2D-CATCH intervention group to those randomized to the usual-care control group to determine whether the enhanced CHW intervention results in greater improvements in HbA1c, CGM uptake, HRSN outcomes, and other diabetes-related and healthcare outcomes over 12 months.

Participants will:

* Receive up to 11 individual Tier 2 CHW sessions focused on HRSN and CGM navigation if randomized to the intervention group. CGM navigation will include: introduction to technology, barrier assessment and goal setting, hands-on device demonstration and training, insurance navigation and prior authorization documentation, and ongoing support to promote continued use.
* Receive routine diabetes care and education and be referred to a standard Tier 1 CHW for HRSN navigation if randomized to the control group. Tier 1 CHWs will meet with participants as needed.
* Complete study assessments at baseline, 3, 6, and 12 months. This includes completion of study surveys and HbA1c laboratory testing. Participants may also be selected to complete semi-structured interviews at 12 months.
interventions: Type 2 Diabetes-Collaboration Around Technology Using Community Health Workers
primary_outcomes: Mean Hemoglobin A1c at Baseline & 6 Months
title: Type 2 Diabetes-Collaboration Around Technology Using Community Health Workers

brief_summary:
In this randomized clinical trial, the investigators will study whether the participants with pancreatic cancer can benefit from starting chemotherapy later than usual after surgery. The investigators will compare two groups of patients:

Patients who start adjuvant chemotherapy between 13 and 24 weeks after surgery. Patients who receive no adjuvant chemotherapy, which is the current standard approach if treatment could not be started within 12 weeks after surgery.

Patients who have recovered sufficiently from surgery between 13 and 24 weeks after their operation, and who show no signs of cancer recurrence or spread, can participate in the study. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups. Patients receiving treatment will be given one of the standard chemotherapy regimens routinely used in clinical practice.

All patients will be followed with CT scans and blood tests for tumor markers every six months for five years.

For patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, the overall survival after surgery is strongly linked to whether they receive adjuvant chemotherapy. Pancreatic surgery is a major operation with a high risk of complications. As a result, many patients do not recover well enough to start chemotherapy within the 12 weeks recommended by international guidelines. These patients are therefore often left without any additional treatment after surgery.

It is currently unclear whether starting adjuvant chemotherapy later than 12 weeks after surgery is still beneficial. Some retrospective studies suggest that delayed treatment may improve survival compared with surgery alone. However, these studies have included relatively few patients and were not designed to provide definitive answers.

The patients targeted in this study represent an important group that has largely been overlooked in previous clinical trials. The question of whether delayed adjuvant chemotherapy can improve outcomes is recognized internationally as a major unanswered research question. Because patients treated with surgery alone generally have poorer survival, it is important to determine whether delayed chemotherapy can still provide meaningful benefit.
interventions: Delayed adjuvant standard systemic chemotherapy given within 13-24 weeks after pancreatic cancer surgery, outside the standardized interval within 12 weeks after surgery
title: Delayed Adjuvant Systemic Therapy Versus Standard of Care (Observation Without Adjuvant Therapy) in Patients Ineligible for Timely Adjuvant Therapy After Resection of Pancreatic Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if d-cycloserine works to enhance the anti-depressive effect of a two day course of accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation (aTMS) in patients with depression. Secondary goals include looking at the durability of the anti-depressive response and assessing adverse effects. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does d-cycloserine improve the depression scaling score compared to placebo?
* What other effects (anxiolytic, cognitive, adverse, durability) do patients encounter with this treatment plan?

Researchers will compare d-cycloserine to a placebo (a look-alike substance that contains no drug) to see if d-cycloserine works to enhance aTMS.

Participants will:

Take d-cycloserine or a placebo two days in a row; each day prior to receiving 20 sessions of intermittent theta beta stimulation (iTBS).

Visit the clinic once every week for the first 6 weeks, and every month until 6 months most weeks for follow-up testing
primary_outcomes: Change in performance on the cognitive test battery at 1 week post-treatment
title: Medicinal Improvement of Brain Stimulation for Depression

brief_summary:
Scoliosis is a condition in which the spine curves sideways. This study compares children and adolescents with congenital scoliosis and idiopathic scoliosis.

The main goal is to determine whether the two groups differ in balance and walking. The researchers will also evaluate spinal measurements, back muscles, physical function, and quality of life.

Participants will be between 6 and 18 years of age. They will complete balance and walking tests and a scoliosis-related quality-of-life questionnaire. The researchers will also review participants' existing X-rays and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans.

The study will help researchers better understand differences in balance, walking, and related physical features between congenital and idiopathic scoliosis.
primary_outcomes: single-leg stance test with eyes closed
title: Balance and Gait in Congenital and ıdiopathic Scoliosis

brief_summary: This retrospective, single-center observational study will include approximately 102 adult patients with autoimmune myasthenia gravis who experienced at least one myasthenic crisis requiring admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) at Nice University Hospital between December 2009 and September 2026. The primary objective is to describe patients' demographic, clinical, and serological characteristics, maintenance treatments received during the six months preceding each crisis, the number of crises per patient, and documented precipitating factors. Secondary objectives include describing maintenance treatment patterns according to the precipitating factors of myasthenic crises, in order to characterize treatment profiles across different contexts, including intercurrent infections, spontaneous exacerbations, and poor treatment adherence. The analyses will be primarily descriptive and exploratory, with comparisons between groups where appropriate. No additional clinical examinations or biological samples will be required, and no direct clinical benefit is expected for the included patients.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a higher dose of vitamin D and zinc, given during the first two months of tuberculosis (TB) treatment, strengthens the body's natural defense against TB bacteria in people with pulmonary TB confirmed by laboratory testing.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Does a higher dose of vitamin D plus zinc raise blood levels of cathelicidin (LL-37), a natural germ-fighting protein, more than the low dose of vitamin D plus zinc?

Researchers will compare a higher-dose group with a low-dose group to see whether LL-37 levels at the end of the first two months of TB treatment differ between the groups. They will also look at the other measures listed in the outcomes section of this record.

Participants will:

* Take vitamin D and zinc by mouth every day for 2 months, at either the higher dose or the low dose, together with their usual TB medicines
* Give blood samples at the start of the study and at the end of the 2-month treatment phase
title: High-Dose Versus Low-Dose Vitamin D and Zinc Supplementation in Patients With Pulmonary Tuberculosis

brief_summary:
Effective postoperative pain management is essential for early mobilization, functional recovery, and patient satisfaction following joint arthroplasty. Although intravenous nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are commonly used for perioperative analgesia, intraosseous administration may provide an alternative route for delivering analgesic medication near the surgical site.

This multicenter, prospective, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy controlled trial aims to compare the efficacy and safety of intraosseous versus intravenous flurbiprofen axetil combined with local periarticular infiltration for postoperative pain management following joint arthroplasty.

A total of 240 patients aged 65-80 years undergoing primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty, unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, total hip arthroplasty, or hemiarthroplasty will be enrolled. Participants will be stratified by surgical procedure and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either intraosseous flurbiprofen axetil with intravenous placebo or intravenous flurbiprofen axetil with intraosseous placebo. Both groups will receive standardized periarticular local infiltration analgesia.

The primary outcome is postoperative pain intensity at rest, measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at predefined postoperative time points. Secondary outcomes include pain during movement, opioid consumption, length of hospital stay, joint functional recovery, patient satisfaction, patient-controlled analgesia use, and adverse events.

This study aims to determine whether intraosseous flurbiprofen axetil provides effective and safe postoperative analgesia compared with conventional intravenous administration in patients undergoing joint arthroplasty.
title: Intraosseous Injection of Flurbiprofen Axetil Combined With Cocktail Local Injection for Postoperative Analgesia in Joint Arthroplasty

brief_summary:
This study examined whether an eight-week soccer-specific cognitive-motor training (CMT) program could improve decision-making skills and soccer-specific performance in young soccer players.

A total of 64 male soccer players aged 15-18 years participated in the study. Participants were randomly assigned to either a cognitive-motor training group or an active control group. The CMT group completed soccer-based exercises that combined physical movements with decision-making demands, including scanning before receiving the ball, recognizing opponents' movements, choosing appropriate actions such as passing, dribbling, or shooting, and adapting to changing game situations. The active control group completed conventional soccer technical training, including passing, dribbling, receiving and turning, and finishing exercises.

Both groups completed three 45-minute training sessions per week for eight weeks in addition to their usual team training. Participants were assessed at three time points: before the intervention, immediately after the eight-week training program, and four weeks after the intervention to examine whether any improvements were maintained.

The assessments included video-based soccer decision-making, decision-making during small-sided games, dribbling and passing under defensive pressure, standard dribbling performance, and computerized tests of working memory and inhibitory control.

The study aimed to determine whether integrating decision-making and movement into soccer training provides greater benefits than conventional technical training and whether these benefits are maintained after the training program ends.
conditions: Soccer-Specific Cognitive-Motor Training, Perceptual-Cognitive Skills, and Soccer-Specific Performance in Youth Soccer Players
title: Cognitive-Motor Training for Decision-Making and Soccer Performance in Young Soccer Players

brief_summary:
Patients who need inpatient cardiac surgery after heart attack can wait up to three weeks. During this time the majority of patients are stable but confined to a ward. Movement and social interaction is restricted.Furthermore the risk of hospital acquire infection increases and it is costly. The virtual ward offers a mechanism to keep inpatients at home. They are contacted regularly by the nursing staff and if there is a clinical issue it is escalated to the relevant team. This trial aims to randomise patients who are waiting to the virtual ward or standard care. The virtual ward patients will be brought back into hospital for surgery the night before or the day of the operation. This pilot study aims to assess the safety of this strategy

In clinically stable patients awaiting CABG following AMI, management via virtual wards will result in comparable clinical safety outcomes to traditional inpatient care, while improving resource utilization.
interventions: Discharged to a virtual ward with remote monitoring and clinical oversight while awaiting urgent cardiac surgery
lead_sponsor: The Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
primary_outcomes: Any adverse events occurring prior to surgery.
title: A Randomized Controlled Trial Assessing the Safety of Virtual Ward Discharge for Patients Awaiting Cardiac Surgery After Myocardial Infarction

brief_summary:
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most common endocrine disorders affecting women of reproductive age and is frequently associated with obesity, menstrual irregularity, low back pain, and reduced quality of life. Although aerobic exercise is recommended as a first-line non-pharmacological intervention, limited evidence exists regarding the effectiveness of Wolly-based aerobics compared with aerobic exercises in improving these outcomes.

This randomized clinical trial (RCT) will be conducted at the central park teaching hospital Lahore. A total of 44 obese women with PCOS will be recruited using a non-probability convenience sampling technique and randomly allocated into Group A (Aerobic exercises) and Group B (Wolly-Based Aerobics), with 22 participants in each group. Both groups will receive baseline physiotherapy treatment followed by supervised exercise sessions three times per week for twelve weeks, resulting in a total of 36 exercise sessions. Each session will last approximately 45-60 minutes. Outcome measures will include pain, assessed by using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), menstrual irregularity, assessed by using the structured menstrual history Questionnaire (MHQ), and quality of life, assessed by using the Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Questionnaire (PCOSQ). Assessments will be performed at baseline and after completion of the 6-week intervention. Data will be analyzed using SPSS version 26.0 with appropriate descriptive and inferential statistics. The findings of this study are expected to determine whether Wolly-based aerobics is more effective than aerobic exercises in reducing pain, improving menstrual health, and enhancing quality of life in women with PCOS, thereby providing evidence for an effective physiotherapy intervention in the management of PCOS
primary_outcomes: Menstrual History Questionnaire for menstural irregularities
title: Effects of Wolly Based Versus Aerobic Exercises in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

brief_summary: This prospective, monocentric, descriptive pilot cohort study aims to describe the evolution of frailty in patients aged 75 years and older treated with immunotherapy for melanoma. Frailty and geriatric parameters will be assessed longitudinally over 12 months. The study will also evaluate quality of life, tumor response, immune-related adverse events, institutionalization, mortality, and caregiver burden, and explore their associations with frailty trajectories.
primary_outcomes: Evolution of frailty according to the Fried phenotype between baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months, including transitions between robust, pre-frail, and frail categories

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine if reducing social media use or increasing deep conversations improves adolescents' mental health and well-being. The participants will be adolescents in the 10th grade at specified rural West Virginia High Schools. Plan is to recruit approximately 400 students. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does reducing social media to less than 1 hour per day improve adolescents' well-being and reduce symptoms of anxiety and depression?
2. Does having one 10-minute deep conversation per day improve adolescents' well-being and reduce symptoms of anxiety and depression?
3. Does reducing social media use or increasing deep conversations show more improvements to well-being than journaling or no intervention?
4. Why do some adolescents benefit from less social media or more deep conversations? What factors help explain this?
5. Do some adolescents benefit more or less than others from the intervention conditions? Participants will be randomized into one of four groups to see whether reducing social media use or increasing real-time conversations improves mental health.

   1. Social Media Reduction: limit social media use to less than 1 hour per day.
   2. Conversation Increase: have one meaningful 10-minute conversation each day.
   3. Journaling: complete 10 minutes of expressive writing each day.
   4. Control: continue usual activities without changing behavior.

Participants will be expected to:

1. Complete surveys at 4 different timepoints:

   1. baseline before week of baseline daily reports (Session 1),
   2. after the two-week intervention and daily reports (Session 3),
   3. 2-week follow-up after Session 3 (Session 4),
   4. 2-month follow-up after Session 3 (Session 5)
2. Complete brief daily reports during a 1-week baseline period and a 2-week intervention period.
3. Follow the assigned intervention for 2 weeks.

With rates of depression, anxiety, and loneliness increasing among adolescents today, this study will provide much needed evidence on whether reducing social media or increasing real-time deep conversations (in-person or on the phone) significantly improves teens' emotional health. This study will also identify what types of teens are more likely to benefit from these interventions and why. If effective, the project would give novel intervention options to help teens develop healthier social habits and improve their mental health.
primary_outcomes: Change in Depressive Symptoms (MFQ-SF Total Score)
Change in Anxiety Symptoms (SCARED General and Social Anxiety Total Score)
Change in Mental Well-Being (SWEMWBS Total Score)
title: Project SOCIAL (Step Out, Connect In-person, Abandon Likes)

brief_summary:
This pilot study will test whether applying a low-dose estradiol (estrogen) cream to the face every night for 12 weeks makes facial skin biologically younger in peri- and post-menopausal women. Skin biological age will be measured with Mitra Bio's skin epigenetic clock, which reads DNA methylation patterns from skin cells collected painlessly with adhesive tape strips.

The study will also look at whether the effect differs between women who are and are not already taking systemic hormone replacement therapy (HRT), whether it differs between peri- and post-menopausal women, and whether adding a topical rapamycin analog (rapalog) serum gives an extra benefit.
title: Epigenetic Modifications Following Topical Estradiol Treatment for Skin Rejuvenation in Peri- and Post-Menopausal Women: A Pilot Study

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to find out whether it is possible to carry out a larger study investigating a breathing muscle training programme for people who have developed swelling in the throat area after treatment for head and neck cancer.

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial compares dexmedetomidine and tramadol as adjuncts to 0.25% bupivacaine in an ultrasound-guided modified pectoral nerve block (PECS II) for postoperative analgesia in women undergoing modified radical mastectomy under general anaesthesia. brief_summary: This is a prospective, single-center, single-operator (Noci Stim) pilot comparative diagnostic study. The study evaluates agreement between expert manual palpation and Noci Stim electrical stimulation for identifying pain-generating muscles in patients with non-radiating low back pain. Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (MRS) is included as an exploratory modality to investigate biochemical correlates of clinically identified pain-generating muscles. The study is designed to confirm device parameters, assess endpoint robustness, and generate data to support pivotal study design.
