brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether applying 2% lidocaine gel to the sampling swab improves detection of human papillomavirus (HPV) in adult men undergoing genital HPV testing. The main question it aims to answer is: Does a gel-lubricated swab detect HPV DNA by PCR more often than a standard dry swab? Researchers will compare a gel-lubricated swab with a standard dry swab to see if the gel increases the proportion of men in whom HPV is detected. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two sampling methods and will have a single genital swab sample taken at one clinic visit (urethral meatus, then pubic, penile and scrotal skin).
title: Lidocaine Gel-Lubricated Swab Versus Dry Swab for HPV Detection in Men

brief_summary:
The goal of this retrospective observational cohort study is to learn how metabolic health factors and the use of GLP-1-related medications affect recovery and complications after major liver surgery in adults undergoing removal of three or more liver segments (major hepatectomy). The study aims to improve understanding of which patients are at higher risk of complications and how care before and after surgery can be optimized.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Is the use of GLP-1 medications (used for conditions such as diabetes and obesity) associated with serious complications after major liver surgery, including post-hepatectomy liver failure? Which patient characteristics, metabolic risk factors, and treatment factors can help predict the risk of complications after major liver surgery? Does GLP-1 medication use influence the risk of breathing complications, including aspiration (stomach contents entering the lungs)? Are metabolic risk factors or GLP-1 medication use associated with longer-term outcomes, such as chronic pain after surgery?

Researchers will compare outcomes between patients with different metabolic risk profiles and different exposures to GLP-1-related medications to understand whether these factors are associated with differences in recovery after surgery.

Participants will:

Not be asked to undergo any additional tests or treatments as part of this study.

Have information from their previous medical care analysed, including medical history, medications, surgical details, anaesthesia management, and recovery after surgery.

Contribute to a large international database of approximately 10,000 patients who underwent major liver surgery between January 2015 and June 2026.

The information collected in this study may help healthcare professionals better identify patients at increased risk of complications and develop improved strategies to prepare patients for major liver surgery in the future.
title: Metabolic Risk Factors and Impact of GLP-1 on Perioperative Outcomes After Major Hepatectomy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a stellate ganglion block (SGB) works to prevent a new irregular heartbeat, called atrial fibrillation, in adults who have heart surgery. It will also learn about the safety of SGB.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does SGB lower the number of participants who develop a new irregular heartbeat in the first 7 days after heart surgery?
2. Does SGB change how often these irregular heartbeats happen, how long they last, and how fast the heart beats during them?
3. Does SGB help participants recover after surgery, for example with less time on a breathing machine, in intensive care, or in hospital?
4. What medical problems do participants have after an SGB? Researchers will compare participants who receive an SGB with participants who do not receive an SGB (they receive the usual care) to see if SGB prevents this irregular heartbeat.

Participants will:

1. Be put into one of the two groups at random.
2. If they are in the SGB group, have an SGB once, on the left side of the neck, with a small amount of numbing medicine. An ultrasound is used to guide the needle, and the block is done after they are asleep for surgery and before the operation starts.
3. If they are in the control group, receive the usual anaesthesia and surgery without an SGB. No study drug is injected.
4. Have their heart rhythm watched continuously for 7 days after surgery, starting as soon as they arrive in the intensive care unit.
5. Have a heart tracing (ECG) recorded every day, plus an extra one if they have chest pain, chest tightness or an irregular pulse.
6. Have a small blood sample (about 2 mL) taken at the end of surgery and on days 1, 3, 5 and 7 after surgery, to check for inflammation and cardiac injury.
7. Have information collected about their hospital stay, such as how long they needed a breathing machine and how long they stayed in intensive care and in hospital.
8. Be checked for any medical problems during the study.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of new onset postoperative atrial fibrillation detected by ECG monitoring
title: Effect of Stellate Ganglion Block on Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery

brief_summary:
The overall objective of this study is to improve the quality and cost-effectiveness of emergency care for older patients attended by Emergency Medical Services (EMS) by supporting frailty-informed, person-centered decision-making in the prehospital setting.

Specific objectives:

1. To improve patient-centered care and patient-reported outcomes for older patients by systematically identifying frailty and supporting a structured dialogue with patients and relatives, including shared decision-making.
2. To reduce the number of avoidable ambulance conveyance to the Emergency Department (ED) and subsequent hospitalizations, thereby reducing healthcare costs, without compromising patient safety or patient-reported outcomes.
primary_outcomes: The primary outcome is the proportion of prehospital contacts that are managed on scene (non-conveyance) without transport to the hospital.
title: Associations of Prehospital Implementation of the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) Combined With a Structured Conversation With Non-Conveyance and Cost-Effectiveness - An Implementation and Quality Improvement Study (WHO-CARES II)

brief_summary: This is a single-center, non-interventional study involving patients undergoing blood sampling within the FRESH program. The study aims to develop local genomic profiling test based on liquid biopsy using NGS. The ultimate objective is to offer this analysis to patients as part of their routine care at Centre Oscar Lambret.
title: Collection of Blood Samples for the Development of Circulating Tumorous DNA Sequencing by NGS From Liquid Biopsies at Centre Oscar Lambret

brief_summary:
Environmental changes represent a major threat to human health by affecting access to water, food security, and air quality. They contribute to the increasing burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases, mental health disorders, and premature mortality. The concept of Planetary Health recognizes the interdependence between human health and ecosystems and highlights the principle of co-benefits, whereby certain interventions simultaneously improve individual health and environmental health.

Within this context, the "12 Months, 12 Actions" project, initially developed in Switzerland, consists of an awareness-raising campaign delivering monthly practical messages aimed at promoting behaviors that benefit both health and the environment. This initiative has already received recognition and has been piloted in primary care settings. Previous experiences have demonstrated (i) its feasibility and (ii) its potential to support health-promoting and environmentally sustainable behaviors. However, its actual impact on behavioral outcomes remains to be evaluated.

The present study aims to implement and evaluate this project in France by focusing on two priority actions because of their potential to improve individual health, public health, and environmental health: reducing meat consumption and promoting physical activity. Despite the importance of these issues, no implementation strategies have yet demonstrated proven effectiveness in primary care settings.

Drawing upon Implementation Science and the PRISM-REAIM framework (Practical, Robust Implementation and Sustainability Model - Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance), the investigators aim to design, test, and implement innovative interventions based on Social Psychology and Social Marketing principles. The study seeks to demonstrate the feasibility of implementing these interventions, the feasibility of assessing their effectiveness, and their potential transferability to other primary care settings.

The project adopts a complex study design structured into four sequential phases, each corresponding to one of the study objectives and guided by appropriate methodological frameworks.

* Phase 1 - Primary Objective: Contextual Analysis Using the PRISM Framework
* Healthcare professionals component: convergent parallel mixed-methods design combining qualitative and quantitative approaches.
* Participants component: explanatory sequential mixed-methods design combining qualitative and quantitative approaches.
* Phase 2 - Secondary Objective A: Integration of findings from both components of the contextual analysis, followed by the development of interventions to be implemented in France. These interventions will be adapted from preliminary intervention prototypes previously developed in Switzerland, together with the design of an implementation plan.
* Phase 3 - Secondary Objective B: Implementation of the intervention implementation plan and preparation of the intervention evaluation process. This phase will follow an iterative process based on (i) interactions within the Steering Committee (COPIL - Comité de Pilotage, Steering Committee) and (ii) interactions between the Steering Committee and participating teams responsible for implementing the interventions within their primary care organizations. An Agile Project Management methodology will be used, relying on an incremental and flexible approach that incorporates continuous testing, rapid feedback, and iterative adaptation.
* Phase 4 - Secondary Objective C: Multi-method pilot study of data collection procedures, including an evaluation of both implementation outcomes and intervention effectiveness using the RE-AIM framework
interventions: Successive quantitative and qualitative study in 4 steps (for primary objective)
Successive quantitative and qualitative study in 4 steps (for secondary objective)
primary_outcomes: PRISM Context Assessment Score Prior to Intervention Implementation
Number of Intervention Components Achieving Stakeholder Consensus
title: Design and Implementation of Primary Care Interventions Supporting Environmental Health Co-Benefits According to the PRISM-RE-AIM Framework

brief_summary: The purpose of this trial is to find out if a single dose of NNC0487-0502 is safe and tolerated in people living with overweight or obesity and to measure how much NNC0487-0502 is in the blood after one injection.
primary_outcomes: Part A: Number of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAE)
Part B: Number of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAE)
title: A Research Study on How NNC0487-0502 Works in People Living With Overweight or Obesity

brief_summary:
This study is being conducted to evaluate the safety and clinical performance of two new catheters for intermittent catheterisation in female/male adults (≥18 years).

The main question it aims to answer is to evaluate complete bladder emptying during intermittent catheterisation.

The study involves two visits to the study clinic over 14 days. During the study only the study catheters will be used and catheterise according to normal routine and not use any other catheters. Subject will be in close contact with the site personnel and must follow their instructions. This is to ensure that the evaluation regarding your experience of the study catheter will be as accurate as possible.

The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency and the Research Ethics Committee have reviewed and approved the study.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of subjects achieving complete bladder emptying
title: An Evaluation of a Hydrophilic Intermittent Urinary Catheter in Adult Male and Female Patients

brief_summary: ARFID (Avoidant Restrictive Food Intake Disorder) is when a person eats only a small amount of food, or only a few types of food. This makes it difficult for an individual to eat enough or have a varied, nutritional diet. This study is testing a new way of organising support for young people aged 4 to 17 with ARFID. The support is split into parts, called modules. Each young person gets the modules that fit them best. The modules use ideas that NHS teams already use. We want to find out if the support works well in the NHS, and if young people, their caregivers and clinicians like it. What they tell us will help us make it better.
lead_sponsor: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
primary_outcomes: The Pica, ARFID and Rumination Disorder Interview ARFID Questionnaire (PARDI-AR-Q)
The Revised Child Anxiety and Depression Scale (RCADS)
Percentage of median BMI for age and sex (%mBMI)
title: Framework for Optimising Care Using a Modular Support Package for ARFID

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the automated oxygen control function, called Target SpO2 Feedback control by FiO2 (TSF), in the HFT750 high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) device for infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). Maintaining optimal blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) within the target range of 90% to 95% is critical for infants receiving respiratory support, as both too little oxygen (hypoxia) and too much oxygen (hyperoxia) can cause serious complications. Currently, healthcare providers manually adjust the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2), which can be challenging due to rapid changes in an infant's breathing. In this crossover study, eligible infants aged 28 days to 1 year requiring HFNC therapy will be randomly assigned to receive both automated FiO2 control (TSF function ON) and standard manual FiO2 control (TSF function OFF) in one of two sequences. Each control mode will be applied for 6 hours, separated by a 30-minute wash-out period, for a total device application time of 12 hours and 30 minutes. Researchers will compare the occurrence of composite safety events (severe hypoxia, severe hyperoxia, or need for urgent medical intervention) and the percentage of time spent within the target SpO2 range between the two modes.
interventions: HFT750 with Automated FiO2 Control (TSF ON)
HFT750 with Manual FiO2 Control (TSF OFF)
title: Safety and Efficacy of TSF Function in HFT750 Device for Infants (TSF-NEST)

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare the effectiveness and safety of two nebulized bronchodilator treatments in adults presenting to the emergency department with acute moderate asthma exacerbations.

A total of 80 patients aged 18 to 60 years will participate in this randomized controlled trial conducted at a hospital in Pakistan. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups. Group A will receive nebulized ipratropium bromide alone, while Group B will receive nebulized ipratropium bromide combined with salbutamol.

The primary outcome will be improvement in lung function, measured by the change in Peak Expiratory Flow Rate (PEFR) from baseline to 60 minutes after starting treatment. Secondary assessments will include improvement in breathing symptoms, requirement for additional rescue therapy, and short-term clinical outcomes.

Participants will be monitored during their emergency department stay for up to four hours or until a decision regarding discharge or hospital admission is made. Adverse events and the need for additional treatment will also be recorded.

The findings are expected to provide locally relevant evidence regarding the comparative effectiveness of nebulized bronchodilator regimens in managing acute asthma exacerbations.
primary_outcomes: Change in Peak Expiratory Flow Rate (PEFR) From Baseline to 60 Minutes
title: Comparison of Two Nebulized Treatments for Acute Moderate Asthma Exacerbations

brief_summary:
Early symptoms of depression and anxiety often emerge during adolescence and young adulthood, yet stigma, limited access to services, and reluctance to seek professional help frequently delay support. This study evaluates DAYA, a self-guided, Malay-language digital intervention grounded in Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), designed to reduce depressive and anxiety symptoms and to improve functioning and psychological well-being among Malaysian adolescents and young adults aged 13 to 24 years. The intervention is delivered through a web-based platform accessible on any internet-enabled device and is completed independently, without direct professional involvement.

The study is a randomised controlled trial conducted in two stages. A pilot trial first assesses the feasibility, usability, and acceptability of the intervention and study procedures. A main trial with new participants then compares DAYA with a waitlist control that receives standard health information. The primary outcomes are depressive and anxiety symptoms, and the secondary outcomes are functional impairment and psychological well-being.
primary_outcomes: Change in depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 total score)
Change in anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 total score)
title: DAYA: A Web-Based Preventive Digital Mental Health Intervention for Depression and Anxiety in Malaysian Adolescents and Young Adults

brief_summary: This study compares case-based learning combined with situational simulation education with conventional lecture-based teaching in the neurosurgery clinical clerkship of a Chinese medical school. Fourth-year clinical medicine students were allocated by the parity of their student identification number to the combined approach or to conventional teaching. Outcomes were a four-part knowledge and skills test, an eight-item questionnaire on the learning experience, and a four-level satisfaction survey.
primary_outcomes: Knowledge and skills test total score
title: Case-Based Learning Combined With Situational Simulation Education in Neurosurgery Clinical Clerkship

brief_summary: This is a prospective, single-arm, self-controlled exploratory study evaluating a 12-month comprehensive myopia-control regimen in 25 children aged 6-12 years with recent-onset myopia (spherical equivalent refraction between -1.00 D and -0.75 D confirmed by cycloplegic refraction). Centered on repeated low-level red-light (RLRL) therapy (650 nm, retinal irradiance 0.01 W/cm², twice daily for 3 minutes each session), the regimen additionally combines: full-focus customized spectacle lenses worn more than 8 hours per day; an outdoor-grade reading lamp providing 4,000 lux desktop illumination; distance-image screen visual training 3-5 times per week; daily nutritional supplements (anthocyanins, DHA, astaxanthin, and vitamins A, D, K); anthocyanin eye patches; and Zijinlong eye drops. Baseline data serve as the self-control. The primary outcome is the change in axial length at 12 months, measured by optical biometry. Secondary outcomes include spherical equivalent refraction progression, macular choroidal thickness, visual function parameters, intraocular pressure, and the incidence of adverse events. Follow-up examinations are performed at baseline and at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. Primary investigator: ZhenFei Yang (Ophthalmology, National Research Center for Rehabilitation Technical Aids, Affiliated Rehabilitation Hospital). Co-Researcher:Kai Cao from Beijing Tongren Hospital
primary_outcomes: Change in axial length from baseline to 12 month
title: Comprehensive Myopia Prevention and Control Therapy in Children

brief_summary: This study is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled clinical trial. Investigators aim to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of remote ischemic conditioning as an adjunctive treatment for hypertension.
primary_outcomes: Change in 24-hour mean ambulatory SBP from baseline to Week 12
title: Efficacy and Safety of Remote Ischemic Conditioning in Hypertension: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Parallel-controlled Trial

brief_summary: When a tooth is removed, the surrounding bone (the alveolar ridge) often shrinks, which can make later dental implant placement more difficult. "Ridge preservation" places a bone graft into the socket at the time of extraction to reduce this shrinkage. This study compared two blood-derived products, each mixed with the same bone graft material, by looking at the healing socket on cone-beam CT (CBCT) imaging. One product was a standardized, factory-made freeze-dried platelet-rich plasma (PRP⁺); the other was a chair-side liquid fibrinogen prepared from the patient's own blood. In each participant, two extraction sites were treated-one with each product-so that the two could be compared within the same person. The main measure was the X-ray density (grayscale value) of the healing socket at 1 and 3 months. This was a small exploratory (feasibility) study intended to gather information for planning a larger trial.
primary_outcomes: Change in cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) grayscale value (GV) at the grafted socket
title: Freeze-Dried PRP⁺ Versus Liquid Fibrinogen for Alveolar Ridge Preservation

brief_summary:
Preoperative anxiety is a common problem among patients awaiting surgery and may negatively affect their perioperative experience. Midazolam, a short-acting benzodiazepine, is frequently used as premedication to reduce anxiety and produce sedation. However, the optimal oral dose for reducing preoperative anxiety in adult surgical patients remains uncertain.

This randomized controlled trial aims to compare the efficacy and safety of two different oral doses of midazolam, 3.75 mg and 7.5 mg, in reducing preoperative anxiety among adult patients undergoing elective surgery under general anesthesia at Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, Karachi, Pakistan.

A total of 120 eligible patients aged 18-60 years will be randomly allocated into two groups of 60 participants each. Group A will receive oral midazolam 3.75 mg, while Group B will receive oral midazolam 7.5 mg on the night before surgery.

The primary outcome will be the difference between groups in the change in anxiety scores from baseline to the preoperative assessment on the morning of surgery. Anxiety will be assessed using a 100-mm Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), where 0 represents no anxiety and 100 represents extreme anxiety.

Secondary assessments will include changes in heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, respiratory rate, and peripheral oxygen saturation.

The study aims to identify which of the two oral midazolam doses provides greater reduction in preoperative anxiety while maintaining acceptable clinical safety. The findings may help guide the selection of an appropriate oral midazolam dose for preoperative anxiety management.
primary_outcomes: Reduction in Preoperative Anxiety Score Measured by Visual Analogue Scale (VAS)
title: Comparison of Two Oral Midazolam Doses for Preoperative Anxiety Reduction

brief_summary: This study compares the effectiveness of two types of anesthesia techniques - caudal block and inguinal field block - in children undergoing genitourinary and inguinal surgeries. It is designed as a randomized controlled trial, meaning participants are randomly assigned to receive either one of the blocks. The aim is to determine which method provides better pain relief and overall outcomes in the pediatric population during and after these surgeries.
conditions: Analgesic Efficacy of Caudal Block vs Inguinal Field Block
title: Inguinal Field Block vs Caudal Block in Children Undergoing Genitourinary and Inguinal Surgeries.

brief_summary: The aim of this randomized controlled study is to evaluate the effects of hybrid midwifery mentorship support on fear of childbirth and mode of delivery preferences among pregnant women expecting their first birth. A total of 64 pregnant women aged 18-35 years who are at 34 weeks of gestation and attend the Obstetrics and Gynecology Outpatient Clinic at Afşin State Hospital will be enrolled. Participants will be randomly assigned to the intervention or control group. The intervention group will receive an individualized midwifery mentorship program consisting of two face-to-face and four online sessions over three weeks. The control group will receive standard prenatal care. Fear of childbirth and mode of delivery preferences will be assessed at baseline and at the end of the three-week program. After childbirth, the actual mode of delivery will be obtained from participants and verified using hospital records.
primary_outcomes: Change in Childbirth Fear Score From Baseline to the End of Week 3
Change in Mode of Delivery Preference Score From Baseline to the End of Week 3
title: MENTORSHIP ON THE PATH TO CHILDBIRTH: MANAGING FEAR OF CHILDBIRTH AND BIRTH PREFERENCES THROUGH HYBRID MIDWIFERY SUPPORT IN PRIMIPAROUS PREGNANT WOMEN

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare the effectiveness and safety of two inhaled treatment regimens in adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) whose condition remains inadequately controlled despite regular treatment.

A total of 220 participants aged 18 to 60 years will be enrolled in this randomized controlled trial conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Pakistan. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups. One group will switch to a once-daily single-inhaler combination of indacaterol, glycopyrronium, and mometasone, while the other group will continue budesonide/formoterol twice daily along with tiotropium once daily.

Participants will receive treatment for 24 weeks, with assessments at baseline, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks. The primary outcome will be the change in lung function, measured by post-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), from baseline to 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes will include changes in COPD symptoms, frequency of disease exacerbations, and treatment-related adverse events.

The study aims to provide evidence regarding the effectiveness and safety of these treatment strategies among Pakistani patients with COPD.
primary_outcomes: Change in Post-Bronchodilator FEV1 From Baseline to Week 24
title: Comparing Two Triple Inhaled Treatment Regimens for Uncontrolled COPD

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the clinical usefulness and safety of a new imaging tracer, gallium-68-labeled carbonic anhydrase IX (68Ga-CAIX), for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging in patients with different types of solid tumors.

Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a protein that is often found at increased levels in certain cancers, particularly in tumors with low oxygen levels. Imaging this protein may help doctors identify and evaluate tumor lesions.

This prospective, single-center study plans to enroll approximately 100 adult patients with solid tumors. Each participant will undergo two PET scans: a conventional 18F-FDG PET scan and an investigational 68Ga-CAIX PET scan, generally within 10 days of each other.

Researchers will evaluate how well 68Ga-CAIX PET identifies primary tumors and metastatic lesions, measure tracer uptake in different tumor types, and compare its imaging findings with those of 18F-FDG PET. Available pathology and clinical follow-up information will also be collected to help interpret the imaging results.

The safety of 68Ga-CAIX will be assessed by monitoring adverse events associated with the imaging procedure. This is a diagnostic imaging study and does not involve experimental cancer treatment.
primary_outcomes: Number of Tumor Lesions With Positive Uptake on 68Ga-CAIX PET
Maximum Standardized Uptake Value of Tumor Lesions on 68Ga-CAIX PET
Mean Standardized Uptake Value of Tumor Lesions on 68Ga-CAIX PET
title: 68Ga-CAIX PET Imaging in Different Types of Tumors

brief_summary: \[68Ga\]Ga-HRS3538 is an investigational radiotracer targeting acid phosphatase 3 (ACP3), a protein expressed in prostate cancer. This prospective, open-label, single-center, single-group phase 1 study will enroll 6 adults with histologically and/or cytologically confirmed prostate cancer who have an indication for ACP3-targeted PET imaging. Each participant will receive a single intravenous injection of 148 MBq (4 mCi) ± 37 MBq of \[68Ga\]Ga-HRS3538, followed by dynamic PET imaging from 0 to 60 minutes after administration, static imaging at approximately 2 hours, and optional static imaging at approximately 4 hours. The primary objective is to assess the safety and tolerability of \[68Ga\]Ga-HRS3538. Secondary objectives are to characterize its biodistribution and radiation dosimetry and to explore its lesion detection and diagnostic performance.
lead_sponsor: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Clinically Significant Changes in Vital Signs
Number of Participants With Clinically Significant Laboratory Abnormalities
Number of Participants With Clinically Significant Electrocardiogram Abnormalities
title: Safety and Diagnostic Performance of [68Ga]Ga-HRS3538 PET in Prostate Cancer

brief_summary:
This study evaluated the effectiveness of hypnotherapy and Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) in managing migraine symptoms and improving psychological wellbeing among university students diagnosed with migraine without aura. Migraine can interfere with academic activities, emotional functioning, stress management, and quality of life.

A randomized, three-group, parallel-assignment study was conducted with 60 university students. Participants were assigned to hypnotherapy, DBT, or psychoeducation, with 20 participants in each group. Each group received six intervention sessions. Hypnotherapy focused on relaxation, guided imagery, pain management, and cognitive reframing. DBT focused on mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion regulation, and interpersonal effectiveness. Psychoeducation provided information about migraine, stress, lifestyle modification, and coping strategies.

Migraine frequency, migraine severity, migraine-related disability, perceived stress, emotional distress, and migraine-specific quality of life were assessed before and after the interventions. The study aimed to compare changes across the three groups and examine the potential usefulness of these psychological approaches for university students experiencing migraine.
primary_outcomes: Change in Perceived Stress Scale-10 (PSS-10) Score
Change in Migraine-Specific Quality of Life Questionnaire (MSQ-14) Score
Change in Robertson Emotional Distress Scale (REDS) Score
Change in Migraine Disability Assessment Test (MIDAS) Score
title: Effectiveness of Hypnotherapy and Dialectical Behavior Therapy for Migraine Among University Students

brief_summary:
Dyspnea is a common and distressing symptom among patients with advanced cancer and may adversely affect physical functioning, psychological well-being, and quality of life. This study aims to evaluate whether a sound-guided meditation program can help relieve cancer-related dyspnea.

In this randomized controlled trial, eligible participants will be assigned to either a 8-week sound-guided meditation group or a health education control group. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, 8 weeks, and 20 weeks. The primary outcome is the intensity of dyspnea at 8 weeks. Other outcomes include multidimensional dyspnea, dyspnea-related functional limitations, psychological distress, health-related quality of life, and pulmonary function. Participants' experiences and views of the program will also be explored.
primary_outcomes: Change in Dyspnea Intensity at 8 Weeks
title: Sound-Guided Meditation for Cancer-Related Dyspnea in Patients With Advanced Cancer

brief_summary:
Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) remains an important route of hepatitis B virus (HBV) transmission, particularly in high-prevalence settings. Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) administered during pregnancy is an effective intervention for reducing the risk of MTCT of HBV. Despite its demonstrated effectiveness, the intervention is not routinely implemented in many high-HBV-burden settings. Generating local evidence on the effectiveness of TDF under routine healthcare conditions is therefore important to inform policy decisions and guide the potential scale-up of the intervention.

A quasi-experimental study will be conducted in the Afar and Oromia regions to evaluate the effectiveness of oral TDF 300mg once daily, administered from the second trimester of pregnancy until three months after delivery, in preventing mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HBV. In three years, a total of 6000 hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positive pregnant women will receive TDF (the intervention group). With expected attrition of 50%, we aim to screen at least 3000 infants born to these mothers as they reach 6-12 months of age. For the historical comparator group, 371 HBsAg-positive mothers and their infants will be required. Screening will be done using the WHO pre-qualified Abbott Determine-2 HBsAg kit to ensure uniform testing procedure across all study sites. The proportion of infants aged 6-12 months who are HBsAg-positive will be compared between the prospective TDF intervention cohort and the historical comparator group. A generalized linear model with a binomial family will be used to report relative risk. An absolute effect measure, risk difference, will also be reported.

This study will generate locally relevant evidence on the effectiveness of maternal TDF administered during pregnancy in preventing MTCT of HBV. By comparing HBsAg positivity among infants aged 6-12 months in a prospective TDF intervention cohort with that in a historical comparator group, the study will provide evidence that may inform policy decisions and the potential scale-up of the intervention in similar settings.
interventions: Maternal tenofovir disoproxil fumarate use during pregnancy
title: Hepatitis B Virus in Ethiopia: Breaking the Vicious Cycle of Transmission

brief_summary:
This multicenter, randomized, sham-controlled pilot trial will evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of 5-Hz temporal interference transcranial alternating current stimulation (TI-tACS) in adults with social anxiety disorder (SAD). Fifty participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive active stimulation targeting the right bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST) or sham stimulation, in addition to usual treatment. Participants will receive three 20-minute sessions per day, separated by 1-hour intervals, for 7 consecutive days (21 sessions in total).

The primary outcome is the change in Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale (LSAS) total score from baseline to Week 1. Secondary and exploratory assessments will evaluate social anxiety and related symptoms, sleep quality, psychological resilience, cognitive performance, treatment tolerability, adverse events, peripheral blood samples, and EEG and MRI measures. Assessments are scheduled at baseline, Day 1, Week 1, Week 4, and Week 8, with assessment components varying by visit. The Day 1 assessment will focus on the immediate subjective response to treatment using a visual analogue scale.
interventions: Temporal Interference transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation (TI-tACS)
Sham Temporal Interference transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation (Sham TI-tACS)
primary_outcomes: Change in Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale (LSAS) Total Score From Baseline to Week 1
title: Temporal Interference Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation Targeting the BNST for Social Anxiety Disorder

brief_summary: This research aims to compare the effects of tele-rehabilitation and in-person physical therapy on pain, range of motion (ROM), and functional disability in patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA). It will evaluate whether remote physiotherapy interventions can provide outcomes comparable to conventional face-to-face treatment. Pain intensity, knee joint mobility, and functional performance will be assessed using appropriate clinical outcome measures. The study will also explore the effectiveness and accessibility of both rehabilitation approaches. The findings may help identify the most suitable treatment approach for managing knee OA. Ultimately, this research aims to provide evidence for improving patient outcomes and quality of life through effective rehabilitation strategies.
title: Effects of Tele-rehabilitation Versus In-person Physical Therapy in Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate the acute effects of different exercise modalities on energy metabolism and 24-hour glucose profiles in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Approximately 25 adults aged 50-65 years with type 2 diabetes will participate in this randomized crossover study. The study will compare responses to moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT), high-intensity interval training (HIIT), and a non-exercise control condition.
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Energy Expenditure During the Post-Lunch Period
title: Exercise and Energy Metabolism in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary: This study will evaluate a stroke telerehabilitation occupational therapy program delivered remotely to adults with arm and hand impairment following stroke. Participants will complete virtual assessments and six telerehabilitation sessions over approximately six weeks. Outcomes from the six-session program will be compared with previously collected data from a historical cohort that received a nine-session version of the program. The goal is to identify an effective intervention duration and inform implementation of stroke telerehabilitation in outpatient rehabilitation practice.
title: Stroke Tele Implementation

brief_summary: This randomized control trial aims to determine the effects of structured Core Canister Training on muscular thickness, lumbopelvic stability and pelvic floor function in pregnant women diagnosed with GDM
primary_outcomes: International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire - Urinary Incontinence Short Form (ICIQ-UI SF)
title: Effects Of Core Canister Training in Pregnant Women With History of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized simulation study is to compare two emergency methods for placing a breathing tube when blood makes the airway difficult to manage. Participants will be licensed paramedics practising in Nova Scotia who are trained and authorized to perform both methods. All procedures will be performed on a manikin, a model used for medical training.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Which method allows paramedics to correctly place a breathing tube more quickly after they are told that breathing support with a face mask is not working?

Does either method have a higher success rate or fewer incorrect tube placements?

Researchers will compare placing a breathing tube through the mouth using a device with a camera, called video laryngoscopy, with placing a breathing tube through an opening in the front of the neck, called cricothyrotomy. Each participant will perform both procedures, with the order chosen at random. The scenarios will include simulated blood in the airway, dim lighting and background noise to represent difficult conditions outside a hospital.

Participants will:

Complete a questionnaire about their training, experience with airway procedures and confidence in performing them.

Complete two simulated emergency scenarios at the IWK Health Simulation Centre, using one method in each scenario, with a break of at least 20 minutes between scenarios.

Have their procedures timed and video-recorded so researchers can assess correct tube placement, unsuccessful attempts and the need for another airway method.

Complete questionnaires about how mentally and physically demanding each procedure felt and which method they preferred
primary_outcomes: Time from Indication to Definitive Airway (T1 → T3)
title: Direct Cricothyrotomy Versus Orotracheal Intubation in Austere Hemorrhagic Airway Scenarios: A Randomized Crossover Simulation Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot clinical trial is to learn whether a virtual reality mindfulness and self-compassion program can be used during hemodialysis, whether patients find it acceptable, and whether it is safe. The study will include 26 adults who have received in-center hemodialysis for at least 3 months at Hôpital du Haut-Richelieu in Quebec, Canada.

The program, called "Toujours Dimanche," combines guided meditation with videos and sounds of nature. Participants wear a virtual reality headset that makes them feel surrounded by natural landscapes. Mindfulness means paying attention to the present moment without judgment. Self-compassion means treating yourself with kindness during difficult experiences.

The main questions are:

Can researchers recruit patients, and can patients complete the planned virtual reality sessions?

How do patients feel about the program, and how well does it fit into their dialysis treatments?

Does the program cause unwanted effects, such as nausea, dizziness, or discomfort?

Researchers will also collect information about anxiety, depression, stress, emotional well-being, physical symptoms, quality of life, and physical activity. This small pilot study is not designed to determine whether the program improves these outcomes. Its findings will help researchers plan a larger trial.

Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups, with an equal chance of joining either group:

Virtual reality group: Participants will use the headset during their regular hemodialysis treatments for 20 minutes, twice a week, for 16 weeks. Each session includes 10 minutes of guided meditation followed by 10 minutes of freely exploring the virtual nature setting. A research team member will help participants use the equipment and will be available during sessions.

Comparison group: Participants will receive an educational brochure about caring for their mental health during hemodialysis. They will be offered free access to the virtual reality program after the study.

Participants in both groups will:

* Complete questionnaires before the program, around its midpoint, at its end, and about 10 weeks after it ends.
* Wear a wrist-worn activity tracker to record their steps, including for 2 weeks before the program begins.

After the final data collection, a sample of patients and nurses will take part in interviews to share their experiences with the program and suggest improvements before a larger study.

brief_summary:
Liver transplantation remains the only cure for patients with end-stage liver disease. Despite continuous advances in medical care, ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) (tissue damage that occurs when blood supply is restored to an area that has been deprived of oxygen) remains a major contributor to complications with the newly transplanted liver. A key factor involved in the development of IRI is reduced nitric oxide (NO) availability in the body. NO is a transmitter the sends signals to protect cells against injury and to maintain healthy blood vessels. The investigators have designed a randomized clinical trial (RCT) investigating the use of inhaled NO to reduce IRI in liver transplantation.

A total of 110 patients receiving a deceased donor liver transplant will be randomly assigned to receive either inhaled nitric oxide or a nitrogen gas placebo during surgery and for up to 24 hours afterward. The investgators will then collect postoperative data from medical records to evaluate indicators of liver cell injury, liver function, and other common post-transplant complications. The investigators anticipate that participants who receive iNO will have reduced IRI injury and better transplant outcomes than those who received the placebo gas.

Participants will be followed for one year after transplantation. The findings will help determine whether inhaled nitric oxide can improve liver transplant outcomes and support its use as part of routine transplant care.

brief_summary:
People with Mal de Débarquement Syndrome (MdDS) can feel as if they are rocking, bobbing, or swaying even when they are sitting still. For some people with MdDS, these sensations ease while they ride in a car or boat and return when the ride ends. This study uses a short ferry trip to find out what happens to brain activity as the ferry starts moving and after it docks.

The researchers expect brain activity to change during the crossing in people with MdDS. They will look at whether those changes are larger in people who feel more relief and whether brain activity returns toward its starting pattern after the ferry stops. They will also compare responses in people whose MdDS began after travel or another motion exposure, people whose symptoms began spontaneously or after another trigger, and healthy volunteers without MdDS.

The study includes women aged 18 and older. Participants in all three groups follow the same study procedures.

* Before the study session, participants complete online questionnaires about their health, symptoms, and tendency to get motion sickness.
* On the study day, participants wear a cap with small sensors on the scalp. The sensors record the brain's electrical activity, a measurement called an electroencephalogram (EEG). The cap only records signals.
* Participants take a round trip on the Sint-Anna passenger ferry in Antwerp, Belgium. Researchers record brain activity while participants sit still before the first crossing, while the ferry is moving, and after it docks. Participants spend short periods with their eyes open and closed as instructed.
* At several points during the session, participants answer short questions about how they feel, including whether they feel as if they are moving and how strong that sensation is.

Two researchers accompany each participant during the crossings. Participants may feel motion sickness during the trip or discomfort from the cap. They can ask to pause or stop at any time. The study aims to understand why symptoms can ease briefly during motion.

brief_summary:
The goal of this Pre-Post experimental interventional study is to determine whether acute cognitive stress may have a significant effect on how the brain processes information when learning a novel motor skill occurs immediately after acute stress.

The study is randomized two group parallel experimental design where participants will be randomly assigned to an acute stress group (induced via completion of an incongruent stroop task) as compared to a control group where participants will complete a comparator task (congruent stroop task).

Participants: will be healthy, right-handed dominant, male and female participants/volunteers aged 17-35.

Primary Research Question:

Does acute cognitive stress prior to learning a new motor skill change the way that the brain responds to acquisition of that skill? To answer this question, changes in the amplitude of somatosensory evoked potentials (SEPs) before and after participants acquire a motor skill will be compared between the acute stress and control group.

Secondary Research Questions:

1. Does acute cognitive stress prior to learning a new motor skill change the ability of the brain to acquire and retain that motor skill? To answer this question changes in the accuracy of a novel force matching task will be compared pre and post acquisition and at retention, measured 24 hours post acquisition between the acute stress and control group.
2. Does acute cognitive stress prior to learning a new motor skill change EEG measured prior to, during and post acquisition as compared to the control group?

Participants will complete the following procedures:

* Complete a pre-lab questionnaire screening to ensure eligibility criteria are followed, as well as signing an informed consent forum.
* EEG measures: a 64 channel EEG cap will be placed on the participant's head using the international 10/20 system. Resting state EEG measures will be collected, and EEG will be collected pre, during an post acquisition of the motor skill.
* SEP measures: Electrodes will be placed over the right median nerve, for the stimulation of the nerve at frequencies of 2.47Hz and 4.98Hz. In addition to the EEG cap to record cortical SEP measures, electrodes will be placed at specific places including Erb's Point, the Trachea, C5, etc, for recording of the spinal and peripheral SEP components.
* Participants in the acute stress group will complete an Incongruent Stroop Task while the control comparator group will complete a Congruent Stroop task. The goal of the task if to identify the colour of the font as quickly and correctly as possible. In the congruent condition the font will be in the same colour as the word e.g. the word will say "red" and the colour will be red. In the incongruent task, the colour and the word will be different, e.g. the word might say "blue" but the font colour will be red.
* Perform a novel force matching task with pre, acquisition, post and retention performance measures collected. To create an individualized force task, participants will first perform a a maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) to normalize the force matching task to their MVC, followed by a familiarization trial, and finally, randomized force matching acquisition trials across four varying blocks, followed by a post-acquisition block and retention measured 24 hours later.
* Participants will have their EEG and SEP recordings measured once again, after the Force Matching Handgrip Task, in accordance with study procedure.
lead_sponsor: University of Ontario Institute of Technology
title: The Effect of Acute Cognitive Stress on Sensorimotor Processing and Motor Learning

brief_summary: Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. Fever is one of the main clinical manifestations of sepsis and represents a self-protective immune response after the host is challenged by pathogens. However, excessive fever may impair cerebral autoregulation, further affect cerebral oxygen metabolism, and aggravate brain injury. It remains unclear whether brain injury in septic patients is attributable to the systemic inflammatory state or to an independent effect of fever itself. Moreover, authoritative evidence for antipyretic treatment is currently lacking in clinical practice; therefore, there is no uniform standard for temperature management in febrile patients. Research on the effects of body temperature on cerebral hemodynamics has mainly focused on the neuroprotective effects of hypothermia, whereas systematic and in-depth studies on how different degrees of fever affect cerebral hemodynamics in septic patients are still lacking. This study aims to continuously monitor cerebral hemodynamics in septic patients under different body temperature conditions using transcranial Doppler ultrasonography in a prospective cohort study. The core research contents include: 1) clarifying the correlation between fever and cerebral hemodynamic status (e.g., high flow velocity and low resistance); and 2) investigating the effects of fever on cerebral pressure autoregulation and metabolic autoregulation and the corresponding thresholds. From the perspective of cerebral hemodynamics, this project reveals the effects of different degrees of fever on cerebral hemodynamics, providing direct evidence-based medical evidence for temperature management strategies in septic patients in clinical practice.
title: Effect of Fever on Cerebral Hemodynamics in Patients With Sepsis

brief_summary: This study evaluates the feasibility, acceptability, and potential use of personalized immersive virtual reality environments (iVRe) as a non-pharmacological support for managing pain and anxiety during the prodromal phase and first stage of labor. iVRe provides realistic or customizable visual and auditory experiences tailored to individual preferences, aiming to promote relaxation, cognitive distraction, engagement, and a greater sense of control during childbirth. The project is integrated into an obstetric care model that prioritizes a positive birth experience and personalized, natural pain-management strategies. Although previous research suggests that virtual reality may reduce pain and anxiety in medical settings and during labor, evidence remains limited, particularly in Italy. The main objective is therefore to determine whether customizable iVRe can be safely and appropriately introduced into childbirth care. The study will also identify the most suitable stages of labor for headset use, potential barriers and facilitators to implementation, and the visual, auditory, and usage features considered most effective in promoting relaxation, well-being, and pain management. The project includes two preliminary exploratory phases. The first involves obstetric and gynecological healthcare professionals who routinely assist women during labor and childbirth. Following a VR exposure session, standardized questionnaires and a focus group will assess feasibility, usability, sense of presence, possible side effects, and methodological considerations for future implementation with women in labor. The second phase involves women approximately 40 days postpartum. Drawing on their recent childbirth experience, participants will evaluate the acceptability of VR and provide suggestions regarding its use. The assessment will include emotional state before and after exposure, headset-related symptoms, usability, engagement, realism, and preferences for virtual content. Expected outcomes include preliminary evidence on the safety, tolerability, usability, and acceptability of immersive VR in obstetric care. These findings will be used to refine the methodology and procedures for a subsequent study involving women during the prodromal phase and labor.
primary_outcomes: Adverse symptoms associated with immersive virtual reality exposure
Change in state anxiety before and after immersive virtual reality exposure
Feasibility and usability of the immersive virtual reality experience
Sense of presence, engagement, and perceived realism of the immersive virtual reality experience
Methodological requirements for a subsequent study involving women during labor

brief_summary:
Arthroscopic medial meniscal repair is a minimally invasive knee surgery that can cause moderate pain after the operation, making early movement and physical therapy difficult. An ultrasound-guided adductor canal block is a targeted nerve block given in the middle of the thigh to numb pain signals from the knee while preserving thigh muscle strength. However, pain relief from a single injection of the local anesthetic bupivacaine alone lasts for a limited time. Ondansetron, a medication commonly used to prevent nausea and vomiting, may help extend the duration of pain relief when mixed with bupivacaine.

The purpose of this clinical trial is to find out whether adding ondansetron to bupivacaine in an ultrasound-guided adductor canal block makes postoperative pain relief last longer than bupivacaine alone in adults aged 18 to 40 years having planned arthroscopic medial meniscal repair under spinal anesthesia.

Participants will be randomly assigned (like flipping a coin) into one of two equal groups. At the end of surgery, all participants will receive an ultrasound-guided adductor canal block in the operated thigh:

* Control Group (Bupivacaine Plus Normal Saline): Receives 16 mL of 0.50% bupivacaine mixed with 4 mL of sterile salt water (normal saline).
* Experimental Group (Bupivacaine Plus Ondansetron): Receives 16 mL of 0.50% bupivacaine mixed with 8 mg (4 mL) of ondansetron.

Neither the participants nor the researchers assessing postoperative recovery will know which mixture each participant received. All participants will be monitored for 24 hours after surgery to measure how long it takes before they first ask for extra pain medication, as well as their pain scores at rest and during knee movement, total amount of extra pain medicine used, thigh muscle strength, time to first assisted walking, nausea and vomiting, overall satisfaction, and any side effects.
primary_outcomes: Duration of Postoperative Analgesia Measured as Time to First Rescue Analgesia Request
title: The Efficacy of Ondansetron as an Adjuvant to Bupivacaine in Ultrasound-Guided Adductor Canal Block for Postoperative Analgesia in Adult Patients Undergoing Arthroscopic Medial Meniscal Repair Surgery

brief_summary:
Sepsis is a life-threatening medical emergency that happens when the body's response to an infection spirals out of control and begins injuring its own tissues and organs. Infections caused by a specific group of bacteria known as gram-negative bacteria frequently lead to severe sepsis and carry a high risk of death, even when patients receive standard intensive care treatments.

The PIONEER Study is a large, real-world observational study being conducted across approximately 150 hospitals and intensive care units in India to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of an approved immune-modulating injection called Sepsivac (which contains heat-killed Mycobacterium w) when used alongside standard medical care. Because this is a real-world, observational study, doctors will treat patients according to their normal clinical judgment; the study itself will not assign patients to different treatment groups or dictate dosing. Researchers plan to enroll up to 15,000 adult patients (aged 18 years and older) with suspected or confirmed gram-negative sepsis who are prescribed Sepsivac alongside standard sepsis care as part of their routine hospital treatment. Each participant's medical progress will be tracked from hospital admission through Day 28 (including by telephone if the patient is discharged earlier). The main goal of the study is to measure overall survival at 28 days (28-day all-cause mortality). Researchers will also collect information on how long patients need a breathing machine (mechanical ventilation), how long they require blood-pressure-supporting medications (vasopressors), how many days they spend in the intensive care unit (ICU), changes in their organ function scores (SOFA score) over time, and any side effects or adverse events that occur during treatment.
title: Pioneer Study: Prospective Indian Open-label Network Evaluating Efficacy and Real-world Safety of Sepsivac in Gram-Negative Sepsis

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to examine the impact of over-the-counter glucose monitoring (Lingo biosensor) to adults with non-insulin treated T2D or prediabetes in a Northern California primary care practice focusing on those of South Asian and Filipino ancestries. Comparisons will be made of (a) the use of the continuous glucose monitor alone or (b) use of the continuous glucose monitor together with culturally congruent, digital-delivered lifestyle education with (c) usual care (including patient handouts and in-clinic medical counseling).

This is a single-center, 3-arm randomized controlled trial (RCT) involving 225 Palo Alto Medical Foundation patients who are of self-proclaimed South Asian or Filipino ancestry. This is a pilot study for OTC CGMs. The study will include three arms, each enrolling 75 participants with an established diagnosis of non-insulin-treated type 2 diabetes or prediabetes, defined as an HbA1c of 6.0-6.4%, to examine changes in glycemic profiles measured by continuous glucose monitoring.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Percentage of Time in Target Glucose Range of 70-140 mg/dL
title: Glycemic Impact of LINGO CGM in Primary Care

brief_summary:
Dietary supplement, gut microbiota and ADHD (short title: Gut microbiota and ADHD) Background and hypothesis ADHD is the most prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder in child psychiatry (about 7.2% of the world population); its aetiology is multifactorial and still poorly understood. The gut microbiota (GM) modulates the gut-brain axis; the 7 available studies report differences in bacterial composition in ADHD, without consensus. Pycnogenol, a polyphenol-rich French maritime pine bark extract, is a dietary supplement (no marketing authorisation, no therapeutic claim) whose biotransformation depends on colonic microbial enzymes. Previous trials show a reduction of ADHD symptoms after 4 to 10 weeks and a very low rate of adverse effects (about 1.8%, minor). Hypothesis: Pycnogenol modulates the GM and regulates the gut-brain axis, improving the clinical symptoms of ADHD and the associated cognitive functions.

Objectives

(1) To identify a possible bacterial signature (dysbiosis) linked to ADHD symptoms and/or associated cognitive functions, by comparing the GM of children with ADHD with that of typically developing children; (2) to explore whether the presumed efficacy of Pycnogenol on clinical symptoms and cognitive functions is associated with a rebalancing of the GM.

Population 100 French-speaking children aged 6 to 12 years inclusive, girls and boys: 50 with ADHD, combined presentation (child psychiatry outpatient clinic, Erasme Medical Center) and 50 typically developing (advertisements, investigators' acquaintances). Consent of the child and of the legal representatives. Exclusion: psychiatric comorbidity, significant eating disorders, lactose intolerance or cow's milk protein allergy, gluten intolerance, prematurity, IQ \< 75, serious chronic disease (IBD, obesity, diabetes, cancer, hepatic/biliary disease, chronic respiratory disease, etc.), vitamins or supplements (omega-3, pro/prebiotics, plant stanols/sterols) within the previous 4 weeks, psychotropic drugs (including methylphenidate), proton pump inhibitors, antibiotics within the previous 3 months. Sample size based on the literature.

Intervention (ADHD group only) Pycnogenol tablets, 1 per day in the middle of the evening meal under parental supervision, for 10 weeks: 20 mg/day for the first 2 weeks, then weight-adjusted dose (30 mg/day if \< 30 kg; 40 mg/day if ≥ 30 kg; 50 mg/day if \> 50 kg). Provided free of charge. The control group receives no Pycnogenol. Visits: T0 inclusion; T1 week 1; T2 week 5; T3 week 10.

Assessments Clinical: DSM-5 criteria and child psychiatric examination (T0, T2, T3); clinician-rated ADHD-RS IV (T0, T2, T3 in ADHD; T1 in controls); Physical Complaints Questionnaire for side effects (T2, T3, ADHD); Food Frequency Questionnaire and Bristol stool scale (T1, T2, T3 ADHD; T1 controls).

Neuropsychological: WISC-V (estimated IQ), TAP battery (visual and auditory selective attention, divided attention, vigilance, flexibility, Go/NoGo inhibition, working memory) and MIDA (delay aversion), at T1 and T3 in ADHD, T1 in controls; Go/NoGo and vigilance also at T2 (ADHD).

Microbiota: stool collected at home (OMNIgene-GUT kit, stable 60 days), stored at -80 °C; DNA extraction (QIAamp DNA Stool Mini Kit), 16S rRNA V1-V3 amplification, Illumina MiSeq sequencing, QIIME2 pipeline. Laboratory and biostatistical analyses: Prof. A. Everard (UCLouvain/LDRI). Biobank: UCLouvain Biothèque (Prof. E. Marbaix); samples destroyed after analysis.

Expected results Replication of a distinct GM composition in ADHD; confirmation of a beneficial effect of Pycnogenol; identification of the cognitive indices most sensitive to it; demonstration of GM modulation correlated with clinical and cognitive improvement.

Data, ethics, risks REDCap eCRF, pseudonymisation by code; the key file is held by the PI only and destroyed after publication. Conducted according to GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki, submitted to the Ethics Committee. Risks: possible mild gastrointestinal complaints or allergy; no incidental findings expected (group-level analyses). No cost to participants; cognitive test results returned to families. Funding: Fund Claude \& Marie-Hélène Lelièvre-Meurée.
conditions: ADHD - Attention Deficit Disorder With Hyperactivity
primary_outcomes: The Maudsley Index of Delay Aversion
title: Gut Microbiota and ADHD.

brief_summary: The CLEAN W.A.T.E.R. - Community-Led Environmental Action for Neighborhood Water Accessibility, Treatment, and Equity Restoration CLEAN WATER Study is a community-engaged research study in the San Luis Valley, Colorado, designed to reduce exposure to potentially harmful metals in drinking water from private wells, particularly arsenic, uranium, and lead. Participating households receive free drinking water testing and personalized results, and eligible participants may receive a free water filtration system to reduce exposure. Over nine months, the study evaluates changes in drinking water quality, urinary metal concentrations, kidney health biomarkers, hydration behaviors, and perceptions of water quality. The ultimate goal is to identify effective, accessible strategies to reduce metal exposure and protect the health of rural communities that rely on private wells.

brief_summary: This prospective, non-randomized, open-label pilot study compared ultrasound-guided greater occipital nerve (GON) hydrodissection using 5% dextrose in water (D5W), ultrasound-guided GON block using lidocaine and dexamethasone, and oral therapy alone in adults with migraine. Participants were allocated to one of three groups and followed weekly for four weeks. The primary outcome was the change in pain intensity on the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) from baseline to week 4. Secondary outcomes included weekly NPRS change, acute post-procedural pain change, responder rates, migraine attack frequency, and adverse events.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a higher red blood cell count helps adults who stay on cardiac support and in a coma after cardiac arrest (when the heart stops). It will also learn if researchers can carry out this type of study on a larger scale. The main questions it aims to answer include:

* Do patients hearts and blood pressure recover sooner if they get blood transfusions to keep a higher red blood cell count?
* Can researchers enroll enough patients, follow the plan for blood transfusions, and reach participants for follow-up questions?
* How many participants survive, and how well do they function 6 months later?

Researchers will compare two ways of giving red blood cell transfusions. A common way to measure the red blood cells in the body is by looking at the hemoglobin level. There will be two strategies for transfusing blood.

* Higher level: Participants will get blood if their hemoglobin level goes below 9 g/dL. For these patients in the higher level group, the goal will be to keep the hemoglobin level at 9 or above.
* Lower level: Participants will get blood if their hemoglobin level goes below 7 g/dL. For these patients in the lower level group, the goal will be to keep the hemoglobin level at 7 or above.

It is not known which strategy is better. A higher level may help because red blood cells carry oxygen throughout the body, and having more of them may help recovery after cardiac arrest. A higher level may be harmful because giving blood transfusions also comes with some risks. Doctors already use both approaches in usual care. Participants will be assigned by chance and have an equal chance of getting either transfusion strategy.

Because patients are in a coma, a family member or legal representative will need to give consent for them.

Participants will:

* Receive blood transfusions determined by the assigned strategy for 7 days
* Have no extra blood draws beyond usual care
* Have their health tracked in the hospital, including how long they need blood pressure medications
* Take part in a phone call at 180 days (6 months) about how they are doing in daily life; a family member or legal representative may answer for them
title: Restrictive vs Liberal Hemoglobin Transfusion After Cardiac Arrest

brief_summary: This feasibility study evaluates whether the SOLID IO platform can generate evaluable assay results from tumor tissue and peripheral blood samples collected from patients with triple-negative breast cancer scheduled for standard-of-care neoadjuvant systemic treatment. Feasibility is assessed based on sample adequacy, successful establishment of the tumor-on-chip platform, generation of a quality-controlled viability readout, and completion of an evaluable assay result within 14 days. The study also evaluates assay success by method, turnaround time, procedure-related adverse events, and exploratory associations between SOLID IO assay results and postoperative pathological findings. SOLID IO results will not be used to guide patient treatment in this study.
primary_outcomes: SOLID IO Platform Workflow Feasibility Success Rate
title: Feasibility of the SOLID IO Organ-on-Chip Platform in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer

brief_summary: The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to learn whether warming the heel with a standardized, evidence-based heel warming protocol before heel lance blood sampling reduces pain and shortens the procedure in healthy term newborns. The main questions it aims to answer are: (1) Does heel warming lower pain scores (Neonatal Infant Pain Scale, NIPS) compared with standard care? (2) Does heel warming change heart rate, oxygen saturation and the duration of blood sampling? Researchers will compare newborns who receive the heel warming protocol before routine newborn metabolic and endocrine screening with newborns who receive standard care without warming. In the intervention group, the heel will be warmed with a thermofor (a soft rubber hot-water bag) in a cotton cover just before the heel lance, following the developed protocol, with skin checks during and after warming. Pain will be scored from video recordings by assessors who do not know the group allocation.
primary_outcomes: Pain score (Neonatal Infant Pain Scale, NIPS)
title: Evidence-Based Heel Warming Protocol for Pain, Physiological Parameters and Procedure Duration During Heel Lance in Term Newborns

brief_summary:
Parastomal hernia is a common complication in patients with a permanent abdominal stoma. It can cause discomfort, difficulty in stoma care, and impaired quality of life. Surgical repair remains challenging because of the risk of recurrence, even after mesh reinforcement. Various laparoscopic techniques, including keyhole, Sugarbaker, and sandwich mesh repairs, have been described, but no single technique has consistently eliminated the risk of recurrence.

The Sasmal-FLARE (Four-Layer Anti-Recurrence Repair) technique is a novel laparoscopic surgical approach designed to address multiple anatomical factors contributing to parastomal hernia recurrence. It combines four sequential steps: (1) obliteration of the parastomal hernia cavity using transfascial sutures; (2) reinforcement of the widened hernia neck by polypropylene suture darning; (3) placement of a composite intraperitoneal mesh in a keyhole configuration around the stomal bowel; and (4) placement of a second intact composite mesh using the Sugarbaker technique, with lateralization of the bowel and adequate mesh overlap. This multilayered approach is intended to reinforce the hernia defect and potentially reduce recurrence.

This prospective, single-centre, interventional pilot study will be conducted in the Department of General Surgery, All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Bhubaneswar, India. A minimum of 10 consecutive adult patients (aged 18 years or above) with uncomplicated parastomal hernia associated with a permanent stoma, who are suitable for elective laparoscopic repair, will be enrolled after obtaining written informed consent.

The primary objective is to determine the recurrence rate of parastomal hernia following the Sasmal-FLARE repair during a follow-up period of 24 months. Secondary objectives include assessing the technical feasibility and safety of the procedure, operative and postoperative complications, postoperative pain, duration of hospital stay, return to routine activities, stoma function, and patient satisfaction.

Patients will undergo standard preoperative assessment followed by laparoscopic repair using the four-layer technique. Clinical follow-up will be performed at approximately 1, 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months after surgery. Hernia recurrence will be assessed clinically, with ultrasonography or computed tomography performed when clinically indicated or when recurrence is uncertain. Postoperative complications, including surgical site infection, seroma, bowel obstruction, mesh-related complications, stoma-related problems, readmission, and reoperation, will be recorded.

As an initial pilot study, the findings will be analysed primarily using descriptive statistics. The study aims to generate preliminary evidence regarding the feasibility, safety, and short- to intermediate-term outcomes of the Sasmal-FLARE technique and provide a basis for future larger clinical studies.

The study has received approval from the Institutional Ethics Committee, AIIMS Bhubaneswar, effective October 27, 2026.
lead_sponsor: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar
primary_outcomes: Parastomal Hernia Recurrence Rate upto 24 Months
title: A Study of a New Four-Layer Laparoscopic Mesh Surgery to Repair Hernias Around a Permanent Stoma in Adults

brief_summary: This observational study will follow 600 community-dwelling adults aged 19 to 80 years who live alone for six months. The study will include 300 participants with mood disorders or elevated mental health risk and 300 comparison participants without major mood disorders, current psychiatric treatment, or elevated mental health risk. The researchers will examine how mental health changes over time and whether these changes are associated with patterns in speech, daily physical activity, and mobility. Participants will attend assessments at enrollment, 6 weeks, 12 weeks, and six calendar months. Assessments will include mental health questionnaires, clinician-rated depressive symptoms, physical and fitness measurements, and recordings of speech and facial video while participants describe positive and negative experiences. Between visits, participants will be prompted to record voice diaries twice daily and complete questionnaires about depression, anxiety, and loneliness every 14 days. With the relevant consent and smartphone permissions, step counts and GPS data will also be collected. Personal health records will be collected at baseline with consent. The collected information will be used to establish a longitudinal multimodal dataset, identify candidate digital markers of mental health, and explore prediction of subsequent symptom changes. No treatment will be assigned by the study, and existing treatment will not be changed by the research protocol. Research-generated artificial intelligence outputs will not be used to automate clinical decisions.

brief_summary:
Diastasis recti abdominis (DRA) affects a significant number of women in the postpartum period. Diastasis recti abdominis (DRA) affects a significant number of women in the postpartum period. The postpartum period often presents challenges such as increased inter-recti distance (diastasis recti), lumbopelvic pain, and reduced abdominal strength.

A randomized controlled trial will be conducted at the Lahore General Hospital and Sehat Medical complex, recruiting 36 participants with 18 per group with postpartum diastasis recti abdominis. The study will use a non-probability convenience sampling technique and participants will be randomly assigned to either Group A (Denizoglu with abdominal splint) or Group B (Denizoglu alone). Exercise and splint sessions will be held three times per week for total duration of eight weeks at low to moderate intensity, adjusted to each participant's tolerance. Participants will asked to perform three sets of 20 repetitions for each exercise, holding a contraction for 5 seconds, followed by 10 seconds of relaxation, for each repetition. Each session will last approximately 40-45 minutes. Inclusion criteria include women aged 20-40 years, with a history of cesarean sections, an IRD ≥ 2cm. Outcome measures include IRD, abdominal strength, and lumbopelvic pain (measured using visual analogue scale) and quality of life measured by using WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire. All data analysis will be performed using SPSS version 27
title: Effects of Denizoglu Method and Abdominal Splint on Lumbopelvic Pain

brief_summary:
Lung cancer is a major comorbidity of ILDs(Interstitial Lung Disease), and patients with ILD are known to be at increased risk of developing lung cancer (LC).

Previous studies on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) have demonstrated a 10-year cumulative incidence of LC in IPF patients of 31.1%-54.7%, thus the coexistence of these two conditions sometimes causes catastrophic outcomes after lung resection. Postoperative acute exacerbation of IPF is one of the fatal complications after lung resection. Mortality after the occurrence of this complication is very high (80%-100%).

The aim of this study is to investigate the surgical and oncological outcomes of patients undergoing lung resection for lung cancer and, more generally, the impact of ILDs on the surgical outcomes of lung resection for lung cancer, identifying the factors that influence prognosis in all fibrosing ILDs.

brief_summary: This controlled quasi-experimental study evaluated the effects of a robotic cat intervention and watching animal videos on psychological and physiological outcomes in older adults with mild to moderate dementia living in a long-term care facility. Participants were assigned sequentially, without randomization, to a robotic cat group, an animal video group, or a control group. The robotic cat intervention and watching animal videos were delivered for 15 minutes, twice weekly for four weeks, for a total of eight sessions. Participants in the control group rested for the same duration without receiving an intervention. Psychological well-being and subjective happiness were assessed before the intervention period, at the end of the four-week period, and again two weeks later. Systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and pulse rate were assessed before and after each session. The study hypothesized that the robotic cat intervention and watching animal videos would have beneficial effects on psychological well-being, subjective happiness, blood pressure, and pulse rate compared with the control condition.
