brief_summary:
This study aims to compare the effects of core stability exercises and task-oriented exercises on balance and trunk control in children with spastic hemiplegic cerebral palsy.

Children with hemiplegic cerebral palsy may have weakness and reduced control on one side of the body, which can affect their posture, balance, and ability to perform everyday activities. Exercises that improve trunk stability and functional movement may help address these difficulties.

This randomized clinical trial will be conducted at Children Hospital, Lahore. A total of 52 children, aged 5 to 8 years, will be included and randomly allocated into two groups of 26 participants each. One group will receive task-oriented exercises, while the other group will receive core stability exercises. Both interventions will be supervised by a physiotherapist and conducted three times per week for six weeks.

Balance will be assessed using the Pediatric Berg Balance Scale, and trunk control will be assessed using the Trunk Impairment Scale. Assessments will be used to compare changes following the exercise programs.

The study will help determine whether core stability exercises or task-oriented exercises are more effective in improving balance and trunk control in children with spastic hemiplegic cerebral palsy.
primary_outcomes: Balance measured using the Pediatric Berg Balance Scale (PBS)
title: Effects of Core Stability and Task-Oriented Exercises in Children With Hemiplegic Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary:
This study will test how well an existing artificial intelligence (AI) model can use photos of the surface of the eyes to tell whether lung nodules are benign or cancerous. The study plans to enroll 1,000 adults at several hospitals in China. Their lung nodules have already been found on a chest CT scan, and their doctors have already scheduled surgery as part of usual care.

The research team will take photos of both eyes before surgery and compare the AI results with the findings from routine laboratory examination of the tissue removed during surgery. The AI results are for research only and will not guide patient care. The study does not require additional CT scans, blood draws, or long-term follow-up.

The findings will inform future studies of whether eye photos could help identify people who may benefit from chest CT screening.

brief_summary:
This study will examine how the type of anesthesia and the gas pressure used during laparoscopic gallbladder removal affect recovery. During this operation, the surgeon uses carbon dioxide gas to create space inside the abdomen. The study will compare low pressure (10 mmHg) with standard pressure (14 mmHg). It will also compare two ways of keeping patients asleep during surgery: medicines given through a vein (propofol and remifentanil) or an anesthetic gas (sevoflurane).

About 140 adults scheduled for gallbladder surgery at Muş State Hospital in Türkiye will take part. Each participant will be assigned by chance to one of four groups and will have an equal chance of receiving each combination of gas pressure and anesthesia. Participants and the researchers who assess their recovery will not know which group they were assigned to.

The main question is how well patients feel 24 hours after surgery. Participants will complete the 15-item Quality of Recovery questionnaire (QoR-15), which asks about pain, physical comfort, emotional well-being, support, and the ability to manage daily activities. The study will also assess nausea and vomiting, the need for pain medicine, and how soon patients can get up and walk.
title: Recovery After Laparoscopic Gallbladder Removal With Low or Standard Abdominal Pressure and Intravenous or Inhaled Anesthesia

brief_summary: This randomized trial will test whether practising with an AI-assisted virtual patient helps third-year nursing students write better care plans and improves their nursing process competency and learning motivation. Sixty students will be randomly assigned to start the practice immediately or after a waiting period. Students will interview a ChatGPT-based virtual patient, prepare their own care plan, and revise it using AI feedback. The waitlist group will receive the same practice later.
title: AI-Assisted Virtual Patient Practice for Nursing Care Planning

brief_summary:
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) has emerged as an alarming global public health challenge over the past few decades. According to the International diabetes federation (IDF), approximately 537 million adults were living with diabetes globally, with the greatest burden increasingly observed in low-and-middle-income countries, especially Pakistan. The chronic metabolic and vascular consequences of T2DM contribute substantially to morbidity, disability, socioeconomic burden, healthcare utilization, and premature mortality.

Type 2 Diabetes-associated Peripheral artery disease (T2DM-associated PAD) is characterized by impaired peripheral circulation and reduced distal limb perfusion, which may contribute to reduced walking capacity, impaired balance, loss of protective sensation, and increased risk of foot complications. These impairments can interact synergistically, resulting in progressive functional decline and reduced quality of life. Early identification and effective rehabilitation strategies are therefore essential to minimize disability and prevent disease-specific adverse lower-limb outcomes.

Exercise therapy is a fundamental component of the management of both T2DM and PAD. Previous research has demonstrated beneficial effects of aerobic, resistance, and combined exercise on glycemic control, cardiovascular fitness, and vascular health. However, much of the existing literature has focused on isolated exercise modalities or conventional combined exercise programs, while evidence regarding the effects of progressive concurrent exercise (PCE) integrating aerobic and elastic band resistance exercise with systematic progression on distal limb perfusion, protective sensation, and balance among T2DM-associated PAD patients has not been adequately established, particularly in Asian populations.

This evidence gap is important because the pathophysiology of T2DM-associated PAD involves multiple interrelated mechanisms, including impaired glycemic regulation, endothelial dysfunction, reduced peripheral perfusion, neuromuscular impairment, and sensory deficits. A multidimensional exercise intervention may therefore provide greater clinical benefits than a single-mode exercise approach.

The objective of the study is to evaluate the effects of a progressive concurrent exercise program on distal limb perfusion, protective sensation, and balance among patients with T2DM-associated PAD pre- and post-12-week intervention. A total of 128 participants will be included in the study. Distal limb perfusion using toe-brachial index, loss of protective sensation via 10g Semmes Weinstein monofilament test, and balance using berg balance scale will be assessed.

In this study, after obtaining informed consent, those who voluntarily agree to participate will be included. Thereafter, participants will be divided into 2 groups. Group A (n= 64) will perform progressive concurrent exercise, whereas group B (n= 64) will perform aerobic exercise for 12 weeks.
title: Progressive Concurrent Exercise for Type-II DM Associated PAD

brief_summary: This is a prospective, randomized (1:1), open-label, parallel-group, phase II investigator-initiated exploratory clinical study with a parallel observational cohort. After screening and signing informed consent, eligible patients will provide tumor tissue for whole-exome sequencing (WES) to test EGFR amplification status. Patients with EGFR amplification will be randomized 1:1 to Arm A (cetuximab plus concurrent chemoradiotherapy \[CRT\] followed by cetuximab consolidation therapy) or Arm B (CRT alone). Patients without EGFR amplification will enter observational Cohort C and receive standard CRT. The primary endpoint is complete clinical response (cCR) assessed by blinded central review. Secondary endpoints include progression-free survival, overall survival, disease control rate, duration of response and safety. A safety lead-in phase and Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) review are planned.
title: Cetuximab Combined With Definitive Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy Versus Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy Alone for Unresectable Locally Advanced Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma With EGFR Amplification

brief_summary:
SwissCardIA is a prospective, observational, population-based cohort study conducted at two university hospitals in Switzerland: Centre hospitalier universitaire vaudois (CHUV), Lausanne, and Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève (HUG), Geneva. The study aims to investigate how cardiovascular risk factors, including lifestyle habits, biological markers, and clinical characteristics, are associated with the presence and progression of coronary atherosclerosis in asymptomatic adults.

The study plans to enroll 2000 adults aged 50 to 69 years without known cardiovascular disease and not receiving lipid-lowering therapy. Participants are recruited from a random sample of the general population of the cantons of Vaud and Geneva.

At baseline, participants undergo clinical assessments, blood sampling, and health and lifestyle questionnaires, followed by three months of smartwatch-based monitoring of physical activity, sleep, and cardiovascular parameters. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is subsequently performed to quantify coronary atherosclerotic plaque burden and composition.

Participants are followed for up to four years to assess cardiovascular events. Subject to continued eligibility, repeat clinical assessments, lifestyle monitoring, and CCTA will be conducted to investigate coronary plaque progression.

The study seeks to improve understanding of early coronary atherosclerosis and support the development of more individualized approaches to cardiovascular risk assessment and primary prevention.
primary_outcomes: Total coronary plaque volume (TPV, in mm³)
Longitudinal progression of total coronary plaque volume
Incidence of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE)
title: SwissCardIA: a Cohort for an Individualized Primary Prevention of Coronary Atherosclerotic Disease

brief_summary: Colorectal cancer is an important and growing health concern in Nigeria which leads to adverse psychological distress, including anxiety, depression, fear of recurrence and uncertainty about survival and on the physical wellbeing of patients. Yet culturally appropriate psychosocial support remains limited and a gap exists to address this urgent problem. There is therefore a critical need to pilot and test the feasibility/ acceptability of an intervention called ": EXercise, nutrition, sleep optimisation and Cognitive bEhaviouraL therapy (EXCEL) to aid resilience and improve the mental and physical health of patients undergoing colorectal cancer treatment. The intervention is a six-session, CBT-informed multimodal intervention designed to improve the mental and physical wellbeing of individuals affected by colorectal cancer. Grounded in the principles of cancer prehabilitation and behavioural medicine, the programme integrates cognitive behavioural strategies with structured physical activity, exercise, nutrition education, body composition management, sleep optimisation, and self-management skills to address depression, anxiety, cancer-related fatigue, and reduced quality of life. Through a combination of psychoeducation, cognitive restructuring, behavioural activation, goal setting, and lifestyle coaching, participants are supported to develop healthier thoughts, emotions, and behaviours while enhancing physical function, treatment readiness, and recovery. In addition to assessing recruitment, retention, intervention engagement, acceptability and implementation feasibility, the study will pilot the proposed outcome measures and data collection procedures to inform a future definitive evaluation.
interventions: EXercise, nutrition, sleep optimisation and Cognitive bEhaviouraL therapy (EXCEL)
title: EXercise, Nutrition, Sleep Optimisation and Cognitive bEhaviouraL Therapy (EXCEL): A Feasibility Study of an Integrative Lifestyle Intervention to Improve Resilience and Wellbeing for Colorectal Cancer Patients

brief_summary:
Cervical radiculopathy is a condition caused by compression or irritation of nerves in the neck, resulting in neck pain, pain radiating into the arm, numbness, tingling, and reduced neck movement. These symptoms can affect daily activities and functional ability.

The purpose of this study is to determine the effects of neural flossing with or without scapular mobilization on pain, range of motion, and disability in patients with cervical radiculopathy.

This study will be conducted as a randomized controlled trial. Participants will be divided into two groups. Both groups will receive conventional physiotherapy and neural flossing techniques for the radial, median, and ulnar nerves. The experimental group will additionally receive scapular mobilization.

Treatment will be provided three times per week for four weeks. Pain, cervical range of motion, and disability will be assessed before and after the treatment period using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), an inclinometer, and the Neck Disability Index (NDI).

The findings will help determine whether adding scapular mobilization to neural flossing provides additional benefits for patients with cervical radiculopathy.
title: Neural Flossing With or Without Scapular Mobilization for Cervical Radiculopathy

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase II study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ESG206 in the treatment of primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP).
title: A Phase II Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Anti-BAFF-R Monoclonal Antibody ESG206 in Primary Immune Thrombocytopenia

brief_summary:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a major health problem, characterized by a rising incidence and limited treatment options. There is an urgent need for in vivo imaging methods capable of reliably determining tumor subtype and of evaluating, from a prognostic standpoint, the response to neoadjuvant therapy in order to guide surgical resection.

The structural and mechanical properties of PDACs vary by tumor type and are likely to influence treatment response. Among MRI imaging techniques, diffusion-weighted MRI is sensitive to the structural properties of tissues, while elastography is sensitive to their mechanical properties.

The MISTRA project aims to evaluate the performance of diffusion-weighted MRI and MRI elastography in determining tumor subtypes and predicting response to treatment.
primary_outcomes: Measurement of tumoral and peri-tumoral ROI size (mm²)
Measurement of magnitude of shear modulus (kPa)
Measurement of real part of shear modulus (kPa)
Measurement of imaginary part of shear modulus (kPa)
Measurement of velocity of shear wave (m/s)
Measurement of shear modulus phase angle (rad)
Measurement of fraction of ROI pixels with high viscosity (%)
Measurement of apparent diffusion coefficient index (x10-3 mm²/s)
title: Identification of Biomarkers Using Quantitative Imaging for Phenotyping and Predicting Treatment Response in Pancreatic Cancer

brief_summary: Preterm infants often experience stress and discomfort during their stay in neonatal intensive care units. Proper positioning may help them feel more comfortable. This study aims to examine whether providing soft foot support improves comfort and reduces stress in preterm infants. A total of 130 preterm infants will be randomly assigned to two groups. Infants in the intervention group will receive soft foot support for six hours. Infants in the control group will receive routine care without additional foot support. Comfort, pain, stress, and body positioning will be assessed before and after the intervention. Sleep duration and feeding tolerance will also be evaluated. The study will explore whether foot support can be a useful part of daily developmental care for preterm infants.
primary_outcomes: Change in Neonatal Pain and Stress Scores
Change in Preterm Infant Comfort Scores
title: Effect of Foot Support on Comfort and Stress in Preterm Infants

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare the accuracy of the Donnenfeld and Nichamin Age- and Pachymetry-Adjusted (NAPA) nomograms for manual limbal relaxing incision (LRI) performed during phacoemulsification cataract surgery in adults with anterior corneal astigmatism. The study also aims to evaluate the pattern of astigmatism correction in the Indonesian population using Alpins vector analysis.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the NAPA nomogram result in a lower postoperative Difference Vector (DV) than the Donnenfeld nomogram? How do the two nomograms compare in terms of other vector analysis parameters (Correction Index, Index of Success, and Angle of Error), residual refractive cylinder, postoperative visual acuity, and procedure-related complications? Researchers will compare manual limbal relaxing incision planned with the Donnenfeld nomogram versus manual limbal relaxing incision planned with the NAPA nomogram to determine which nomogram provides more accurate astigmatism correction in Indonesian patients undergoing cataract surgery.

Participants will:

Undergo preoperative ophthalmic examinations, including corneal topography, keratometry, pachymetry, and refraction.

Be randomly assigned to receive manual limbal relaxing incision planned using either the Donnenfeld nomogram or the NAPA nomogram during phacoemulsification cataract surgery.

Attend scheduled postoperative follow-up visits for assessment of visual acuity, refractive outcomes, corneal astigmatism, and vector analysis parameters, including Difference Vector (DV), Correction Index (CI), Index of Success (IOS), and Angle of Error (AE), as well as monitoring for procedure-related complications.
interventions: Manual Limbal Relaxing Incision NAPA nomogram
title: Comparison of Donnenfeld and NAPA Nomograms for Manual Limbal Relaxing Incision in Corneal Astigmatism Correction During Phacoemulsification

brief_summary: Children with IgA nephropathy, or with IgA vasculitis that has affected the kidneys, often lose protein in their urine, and over many years this can damage the kidneys. Steroid medicines are commonly used to reduce the inflammation, but in children they can cause serious side effects, including slowed growth. This study will give budesonide enteric-coated capsules once a day, for 9 months, to 20 children who also receive standard treatment that does not include steroid tablets. To see whether the capsules help, these children will be compared with 20 similar children who were treated at this hospital in the past and who did not receive the capsules; their information will come from their medical records and their names will not be used. The capsules are approved for adults only, so their use in children is outside the approved label. We will measure protein in the urine and check for side effects.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in 24-hour urinary protein excretion at week 36
title: Budesonide Enteric-Coated Capsules for Children With IgA Nephropathy or IgA Vasculitis Nephritis
